# Plan: Add Nostr DM Channel Support

**Issue:** [moltis-org/moltis#668](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/issues/668)

## Context

Moltis supports six messaging channels (Telegram, Discord, Slack, MS Teams, WhatsApp, Matrix) but none are decentralized or censorship-resistant. Users who rely on Nostr have no native path to connect. The openclaw project (TypeScript) already ships a production Nostr channel (~8K LOC) with NIP-01/NIP-04 support, relay health tracking, circuit breakers, OTP/allowlist access control, and profile management. This plan ports the concept to Rust using `nostr-sdk` v0.44 (tokio-native, NIP-04 + NIP-44 built-in).

## Scope — What "comparable with other channels" means

To reach parity with the minimum bar from the channel integration checklist:

| Capability | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Inbound DMs | Must-have | NIP-04 encrypted DMs (kind:4), NIP-44 when sender supports it |
| Outbound text replies | Must-have | Encrypted reply to sender pubkey |
| Streaming responses | Must-have | Edit-in-place not possible on Nostr; stream internally, send final |
| DM policy + allowlist | Must-have | `open`, `allowlist`, `pairing`, `disabled` — by pubkey |
| OTP approval flow | Must-have | Unknown senders get a pairing code DM |
| Typed config + redacted export | Must-have | `NostrAccountConfig` struct |
| Web UI add/edit flows | Must-have | Settings page + advanced JSON editor |
| Config template + docs | Must-have | Same PR |
| Relay health + reconnect | Must-have | `nostr-sdk` Client handles reconnect; add circuit-breaker metrics |
| NIP-01 profile (kind:0) | Nice-to-have | Publish bot profile metadata on start |
| NIP-65 relay list | Nice-to-have | Future — advertise preferred relays |
| Media attachments | Nice-to-have | Future — NIP-94 file metadata |
| Reactions (NIP-25) | Nice-to-have | Future |

## Architecture

### Crate: `crates/nostr/`

```
crates/nostr/
├── Cargo.toml
└── src/
    ├── lib.rs            # Re-exports NostrPlugin
    ├── plugin.rs         # ChannelPlugin trait impl, account lifecycle
    ├── config.rs         # NostrAccountConfig, RedactedConfig, defaults
    ├── bus.rs            # Relay subscription loop, inbound event pipeline
    ├── outbound.rs       # ChannelOutbound impl (encrypt + publish DM)
    ├── access.rs         # Allowlist + OTP gating (reuse moltis_channels::gating)
    ├── keys.rs           # Key parsing (nsec/hex), validation, pubkey derivation
    ├── seen.rs           # LRU dedup tracker for event IDs (prevent replay)
    ├── error.rs          # NostrError with is_retryable() classification
    └── profile.rs        # NIP-01 profile publish (kind:0)
```

### Key dependency

```toml
# workspace Cargo.toml
nostr-sdk = "0.44"

# crates/nostr/Cargo.toml
[dependencies]
nostr-sdk = { workspace = true }
async-trait = { workspace = true }

moltis-common = { workspace = true }

```

### Feature flag: `nostr` in `crates/gateway/Cargo.toml` and `crates/cli/Cargo.toml`

Gated like Matrix/WhatsApp — enabled by default in CLI.

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1: Scaffold crate + ChannelType variant

**Files to modify:**
- `Cargo.toml` (root) — add `moltis-nostr` to workspace members + dependencies
- `crates/nostr/Cargo.toml` — new
- `crates/channels/src/plugin.rs` — add `Nostr` variant to `ChannelType` enum
  - `as_str() → "nostr"`
  - `display_name() → "Nostr"`
  - `secret_fields() → &["secret_key"]`
  - `classify_chat()` → always `Some("dm")` (Nostr DMs are always 1:1)
  - `descriptor()` with capabilities:
    ```rust
    ChannelCapabilities {
        inbound_mode: InboundMode::GatewayLoop, // persistent relay subscription
        supports_outbound: true,
        supports_streaming: false, // no edit-in-place on Nostr
        supports_interactive: false,
        supports_threads: false,
        supports_voice_ingest: false,
        supports_pairing: false,
        supports_otp: true,
        supports_reactions: false,
        supports_location: false,
    }
    ```
  - Update `FromStr`, `ALL`, serde aliases

### Step 2: Config (`config.rs`, `keys.rs`)

```rust
pub struct NostrAccountConfig {
    pub secret_key: Secret<String>,     // nsec1... or 64-char hex
    pub relays: Vec<String>,            // wss:// URLs, defaults to damus+nos.lol
    pub dm_policy: DmPolicy,            // open | allowlist | pairing | disabled
    pub allowed_pubkeys: Vec<String>,   // npub1... or hex
    pub enabled: bool,
    pub profile: Option<NostrProfile>,  // NIP-01 metadata to publish
}

pub struct NostrProfile {
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub display_name: Option<String>,
    pub about: Option<String>,
    pub picture: Option<String>,        // HTTPS URL
    pub nip05: Option<String>,
}
```

Key validation in `keys.rs`:
- Accept `nsec1...` (bech32) or 64-char hex
- Derive public key from secret key
- Normalize pubkeys in allowlist (npub1 → hex)

**Files to modify:**
- `crates/config/src/schema.rs` — add `nostr` to `ChannelsConfig`
- `crates/config/src/validate.rs` — add to `build_schema_map()` channels field
- `crates/config/src/template.rs` — add commented `[channels.nostr]` example

### Step 3: Event bus / subscription loop (`bus.rs`)

Core inbound pipeline (mirrors openclaw's `nostr-bus.ts`):

```
1. nostr-sdk Client subscribes: Filter { kinds: [4], p: [bot_pubkey], since }
2. Event received →
3. Dedup check (LRU seen tracker by event ID)
4. Skip self-messages (event.pubkey == bot_pubkey)
5. Skip stale events (created_at < since)
6. Verify event signature (nostr-sdk does this, but belt-and-suspenders)
7. Authorize sender (allowlist / OTP check) — BEFORE decrypt
8. Decrypt content (NIP-04 or NIP-44 based on event structure)
9. Size validation on plaintext
10. Dispatch to gateway via ChannelEventSink::dispatch_to_chat()
```

The bus runs as a `tokio::spawn` task per account. Cancellation via `CancellationToken`.

### Step 4: Outbound (`outbound.rs`)

Implement `ChannelOutbound`:
- `send_text(account_id, to_pubkey, text, reply_to)`:
  - Look up sender's secret key
  - Encrypt with NIP-04 (broad compat) or NIP-44
  - Build kind:4 event with p-tag
  - Publish via `client.send_event()`
- Error classification: relay failures → retryable; key/encrypt errors → not retryable

### Step 5: Access control (`access.rs`)

Reuse `moltis_channels::gating::{DmPolicy, check_dm_access}` patterns:
- `allowlist` — only allowed pubkeys
- `pairing` — unknown senders get an OTP code via DM, approved in web UI
- `open` — anyone can DM
- `disabled` — ignore all inbound

Implement `ChannelOtpProvider` for the OTP flow.

### Step 6: Plugin lifecycle (`plugin.rs`)

```rust
impl ChannelPlugin for NostrPlugin {
    async fn start_account(id, config) → start Client, connect relays, spawn bus loop
    async fn stop_account(id)           → cancel bus loop, disconnect
    async fn has_account(id) → bool
    async fn account_ids() → Vec<String>
    fn channel_type() → ChannelType::Nostr
    fn outbound() → NostrOutbound
    fn status() → NostrStatus (probe relays)
    fn as_otp_provider() → Some(self)
}
```

### Step 7: Seen tracker (`seen.rs`)

LRU cache of event IDs to prevent replay on relay reconnect:
- Capacity: 100K entries
- TTL: 1 hour
- Persisted to `data_dir()/nostr_seen.json` with debounced writes

### Step 8: Gateway registration

**Files to modify:**
- `crates/gateway/Cargo.toml` — add `moltis-nostr` optional dep + `nostr` feature
- `crates/gateway/src/server.rs` — register NostrPlugin under `#[cfg(feature = "nostr")]`
- `crates/cli/Cargo.toml` — add `nostr` to default features

### Step 9: Web UI

**Files to modify:**
- `crates/web/src/assets/js/page-channels.js` — add Nostr add/edit flow
  - Fields: secret key (password input), relays (comma-separated), DM policy dropdown, allowed pubkeys textarea
  - Show derived npub as read-only after key entry
- `crates/web/src/assets/js/locales/en/channels.js` — Nostr labels
- `crates/web/src/assets/js/channel-utils.js` — validation for nsec/hex format

### Step 10: Config template + docs

- `crates/config/src/template.rs` — add `[channels.nostr]` section
- `docs/src/channels/nostr.md` — new page
- `docs/src/channels.md` — add Nostr to channel list
- `docs/src/SUMMARY.md` — add entry

### Step 11: Tests

- **Unit tests** in `crates/nostr/src/`:
  - `keys.rs` — nsec/hex parsing, pubkey derivation, validation edge cases
  - `config.rs` — defaults, redacted output, merge semantics
  - `access.rs` — allowlist matching, DM policy enforcement
  - `seen.rs` — LRU eviction, TTL expiry, dedup correctness
  - `bus.rs` — event pipeline filtering (stale, self, wrong-kind)
- **Contract tests** — run `moltis_channels::contract` test suite against NostrPlugin
- **E2E tests** — Playwright specs for web UI add/edit flow (`crates/web/ui/e2e/specs/channels-nostr.spec.js`)

## NIP-04 vs NIP-44 Decision

Start with **NIP-04** (kind:4) for broad compatibility — it's what most Nostr clients use today for DMs. Add NIP-44 decryption support for inbound (detect by content format) so the bot can receive NIP-44 encrypted messages. Outbound defaults to NIP-04 for now with a config option to prefer NIP-44.

NIP-17 (gift-wrapped DMs) is a future enhancement — it requires more complex event handling and is less widely supported.

## COMPREHENSIVE CHANNEL PLUGIN ARCHITECTURE EXPLORATION

Based on my thorough exploration of the Moltis codebase, here is the complete channel plugin architecture:

### 1. CHANNELTYPE ENUM

**Location**: `/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/helix-epoch/crates/channels/src/plugin.rs`, lines 16-24

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum ChannelType {
    Telegram,
    Whatsapp,
    #[serde(rename = "msteams")]
    MsTeams,
    Discord,
    Slack,
    Matrix,
}
```

**Key Methods**:
- `as_str(&self) -> &'static str` (lines 28-37) — Returns lowercase identifier ("telegram", "discord", etc.)
- `display_name(&self) -> &'static str` (lines 40-49) — Human-readable names for UI ("Telegram", "Discord", etc.)
- `classify_chat(&self, chat_id: &str) -> Option<String>` (lines 52-66) — Best-effort chat classification (currently only Telegram: "channel_or_supergroup", "group", or "private")
- `secret_fields(&self) -> &'static [&'static str]` (lines 69-78) — Top-level config fields to treat as persisted secrets:
  - Telegram: `["token"]`
  - WhatsApp: `[]`
  - MsTeams: `["app_password", "webhook_secret"]`
  - Discord: `["token"]`
  - Slack: `["bot_token", "app_token", "signing_secret"]`
  - Matrix: `["access_token", "password"]`
- `Display` impl (lines 81-85) — Formats as `as_str()` output
- `FromStr` impl (lines 87-103) — Parses from string, supports aliases like "microsoft_teams", "element" (Matrix), "teams"
- `descriptor(&self) -> ChannelDescriptor` (lines 118-217) — Returns static descriptor with capabilities for each type
- `ALL: &[ChannelType]` (lines 107-114) — All known channel types

### 4. CHANNELEVENT ENUM (Pub/Sub)

**Location**: lines 263-331

Emitted by channels for real-time UI updates:
- `InboundMessage { channel_type, account_id, peer_id, username, sender_name, message_count, access_granted }`

- `PairingComplete { channel_type, account_id, display_name }`
- `PairingFailed { channel_type, account_id, reason }`

### 5. CHANNELEVENTSINK TRAIT

**Location**: lines 333-453

Core event dispatcher — the gateway provides concrete implementation.

**Methods**:
- `async fn emit(&self, event: ChannelEvent)` — Broadcast to UI
- `async fn dispatch_to_chat(&self, text: &str, reply_to: ChannelReplyTarget, meta: ChannelMessageMeta)` — Send message to chat session (like web UI input)
- `async fn dispatch_command(&self, command: &str, reply_to: ChannelReplyTarget) -> Result<String>` — Execute slash command, return text result
- `async fn request_disable_account(&self, channel_type: &str, account_id: &str, reason: &str)` — Request disabling account
- `async fn request_sender_approval(&self, channel_type: &str, account_id: &str, identifier: &str)` — OTP self-approval request (optional default impl)
- `async fn save_channel_voice(&self, audio_data: &[u8], filename: &str, reply_to: &ChannelReplyTarget) -> Option<String>` — Save voice to session media (optional)
- `async fn transcribe_voice(&self, audio_data: &[u8], format: &str) -> Result<String>` — STT transcription (optional)
- `async fn voice_stt_available(&self) -> bool` — Is voice STT configured? (optional, default true)
- `async fn update_location(&self, reply_to: &ChannelReplyTarget, latitude: f64, longitude: f64) -> bool` — Update geolocation (optional)
- `async fn resolve_pending_location(&self, reply_to: &ChannelReplyTarget, latitude: f64, longitude: f64) -> bool` — Resolve tool-triggered location request (optional)
- `async fn dispatch_interaction(&self, callback_data: &str, reply_to: ChannelReplyTarget) -> Result<String>` — Button/menu callback (optional)
- `async fn dispatch_to_chat_with_attachments(&self, text: &str, attachments: Vec<ChannelAttachment>, reply_to: ChannelReplyTarget, meta: ChannelMessageMeta)` — Send multimodal message with images/files (optional, default ignores attachments)

### 6. CHANNELPLUGIN TRAIT

**Location**: lines 633-709

Core channel plugin interface — each messaging platform implements this.

**Core Methods**:
- `fn id(&self) -> &str` — Channel identifier ("telegram", "discord", etc.)

- `fn status(&self) -> Option<&dyn ChannelStatus>` — Get health probe adapter
- `fn has_account(&self, account_id: &str) -> bool`

- `fn account_config(&self, account_id: &str) -> Option<Box<dyn ChannelConfigView>>` — Typed config view
- `fn update_account_config(&self, account_id: &str, config: serde_json::Value) -> Result<()>` — Update config in-memory (without restart)
- `fn shared_outbound(&self) -> Arc<dyn ChannelOutbound>` — Shared outbound for routing outside plugin
- `fn shared_stream_outbound(&self) -> Arc<dyn ChannelStreamOutbound>` — Shared streaming outbound
- `fn account_config_json(&self, account_id: &str) -> Option<serde_json::Value>` — Raw JSON config (for API)

### 24. EXAMPLE: SLACK WEBHOOK VERIFIER

**File**: `/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/helix-epoch/crates/slack/src/channel_webhook_verifier.rs`

**Pattern** (lines 19-86):
```rust
pub struct SlackChannelWebhookVerifier {
    signing_secret: Secret<String>,
}

impl ChannelWebhookVerifier for SlackChannelWebhookVerifier {
    fn verify(&self, headers: &HeaderMap, body: &[u8]) -> Result<VerifiedChannelWebhook, ChannelWebhookRejection> {
        let timestamp = headers.get("x-slack-request-timestamp").ok_or(...)?;
        let signature = headers.get("x-slack-signature").ok_or(...)?;
        
        if !verify_signature(self.signing_secret.expose_secret(), timestamp, body, signature) {
            return Err(ChannelWebhookRejection::BadSignature(...));
        }
        
        let idempotency_key = serde_json::from_slice::<serde_json::Value>(body)
            .ok()
            .and_then(|v| v.get("event_id").and_then(|e| e.as_str()).map(String::from));
        
        let timestamp_epoch = timestamp.parse::<i64>().ok();
        
        Ok(VerifiedChannelWebhook {
            idempotency_key,
            body: Bytes::copy_from_slice(body),
            timestamp_epoch,
        })
    }
    
    fn rate_policy(&self) -> ChannelWebhookRatePolicy {
        ChannelWebhookRatePolicy {
            max_requests_per_minute: 30,
            burst: 10,
        }
    }
    
    fn channel_type(&self) -> ChannelType {
        ChannelType::Slack
    }
}
```

   223→/// How a channel receives inbound messages.
   224→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, serde::Serialize)]
   225→#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
   226→pub enum InboundMode {

   228→    None,
   229→    /// Long-polling loop (Telegram).
   230→    Polling,
   231→    /// Persistent gateway/WebSocket connection (Discord, WhatsApp).
   232→    GatewayLoop,
   233→    /// Socket Mode connection (Slack).
   234→    SocketMode,
   235→    /// HTTP webhook endpoint (Microsoft Teams).
   236→    Webhook,
   237→}
   238→
   239→/// Static capability flags for a channel type.
   240→#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize)]

  1437→            ("slack", &self.slack),

  1441→    /// Iterate all channel configs (named + extra) as `(channel_type, accounts)` pairs.

     1→//! Configuration validation engine.
     2→//!
     3→//! Validates TOML configuration files against the known schema, detects
     4→//! unknown/misspelled fields, and reports security warnings.
     5→
     6→use std::{collections::HashMap, path::Path};
     7→
     8→use secrecy::ExposeSecret;
     9→
    10→use crate::schema::MoltisConfig;
    11→
    12→/// Severity level for a diagnostic.
    13→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
    14→pub enum Severity {
    15→    Error,
    16→    Warning,
    17→    Info,
    18→}
    19→
    20→impl std::fmt::Display for Severity {
    21→    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
    22→        match self {
    23→            Self::Error => write!(f, "error"),
    24→            Self::Warning => write!(f, "warning"),
    25→            Self::Info => write!(f, "info"),
    26→        }
    27→    }
    28→}
    29→
    30→/// A single validation diagnostic.
    31→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    32→pub struct Diagnostic {
    33→    pub severity: Severity,
    34→    /// Category: "syntax", "unknown-field", "deprecated-field", "unknown-provider", "type-error",
    35→    /// "security", "file-ref"
    36→    pub category: &'static str,
    37→    /// Dotted path, e.g. "server.bnd"
    38→    pub path: String,
    39→    pub message: String,
    40→}
    41→
    42→/// Result of validating a configuration file.
    43→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    44→pub struct ValidationResult {
    45→    pub diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>,
    46→    pub config_path: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
    47→}
    48→
    49→impl ValidationResult {
    50→    /// Returns `true` if any diagnostic is an error.
    51→    #[must_use]
    52→    pub fn has_errors(&self) -> bool {
    53→        self.diagnostics
    54→            .iter()
    55→            .any(|d| d.severity == Severity::Error)
    56→    }
    57→
    58→    /// Count diagnostics by severity.
    59→    #[must_use]
    60→    pub fn count(&self, severity: Severity) -> usize {
    61→        self.diagnostics
    62→            .iter()
    63→            .filter(|d| d.severity == severity)
    64→            .count()
    65→    }
    66→}
    67→
    68→// ── Schema tree for unknown-field detection ─────────────────────────────────
    69→
    70→/// Represents the expected shape of the configuration schema.
    71→enum KnownKeys {
    72→    /// A struct with fixed field names.
    73→    Struct(HashMap<&'static str, KnownKeys>),
    74→    /// A map with dynamic keys (providers, mcp.servers, etc.) whose values
    75→    /// have a known shape.
    76→    Map(Box<KnownKeys>),
    77→    /// A map with dynamic keys plus explicit static keys.
    78→    MapWithFields {
    79→        value: Box<KnownKeys>,
    80→        fields: HashMap<&'static str, KnownKeys>,
    81→    },
    82→    /// An array of typed items.
    83→    Array(Box<KnownKeys>),
    84→    /// Scalar value — stop recursion.
    85→    Leaf,
    86→}
    87→
    88→/// Known LLM provider names for hint diagnostics.
    89→const KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES: &[&str] = &[
    90→    "anthropic",

    94→    "xai",

    98→    "openrouter",
    99→    "cerebras",
   100→    "minimax",

   110→/// Build the full schema map mirroring every field in `schema.rs`.
   111→fn build_schema_map() -> KnownKeys {
   112→    use KnownKeys::{Array, Leaf, Map, MapWithFields, Struct};
   113→
   114→    let provider_entry = || {

   140→    let wasm_tool_limits = || {

Now I understand the full picture. Let me compile a comprehensive summary based on what I've found.

## Summary of Matrix Channel Implementation

### 1. **Cargo.toml** (`/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/helix-epoch/crates/matrix/Cargo.toml`)
- Depends on: `matrix-sdk`, `moltis-channels`, `moltis-common`, `moltis-config`
- Optional feature `metrics` for telemetry
- No default features

### 2. **lib.rs** (`/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/helix-epoch/crates/matrix/src/lib.rs`)
Minimal module exports:
```rust
pub mod access;
pub mod client;
pub mod config;
pub mod error;
pub mod handler;
pub mod outbound;
pub mod plugin;
pub mod state;
pub mod verification;

pub use plugin::MatrixPlugin;
```

### 3. **config.rs** (`/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/helix-epoch/crates/matrix/src/config.rs`)

**MatrixAccountConfig** struct with:
- `homeserver: String` — required
- `access_token: Secret<String>` — required, redacted in Debug/display
- `password: Option<Secret<String>>` — optional alt auth
- `user_id, device_id, device_display_name: Option<String>`
- `ownership_mode: MatrixOwnershipMode` (UserManaged | MoltisOwned)
- `dm_policy: DmPolicy`, `room_policy: GroupPolicy`, `mention_mode: MentionMode`
- `room_allowlist, user_allowlist: Vec<String>`
- `auto_join: AutoJoinPolicy` (Always | Allowlist | Off)
- `model, model_provider: Option<String>` — per-account defaults
- `stream_mode: StreamMode` (EditInPlace | Off)
- `edit_throttle_ms: u64`, `stream_min_initial_chars: usize`
- `channel_overrides: HashMap<room_id, ChannelOverride>` — per-room model overrides
- `user_overrides: HashMap<user_id, UserOverride>` — per-user model overrides
- `reply_to_message: bool`
- `ack_reaction: Option<String>` — emoji while processing
- `otp_self_approval: bool`, `otp_cooldown_secs: u64`

**RedactedConfig** wrapper — serializes secrets as `"[REDACTED]"` for API responses.

**ChannelConfigView impl**:
```rust
fn allowlist(&self) -> &[String]                          // user_allowlist
fn group_allowlist(&self) -> &[String]                   // room_allowlist
fn dm_policy(&self) -> DmPolicy
fn group_policy(&self) -> GroupPolicy
fn model(&self) -> Option<&str>
fn model_provider(&self) -> Option<&str>
fn channel_model(&self, channel_id: &str) -> Option<&str>
fn channel_model_provider(&self, channel_id: &str) -> Option<&str>
fn user_model(&self, user_id: &str) -> Option<&str>
fn user_model_provider(&self, user_id: &str) -> Option<&str>
```

**NOTE:** Test at line 440 calls `cfg.resolve_model(room_id, user_id)` — **this method is missing from the impl** (test expects user override > room override > default, returning `Some("user-model")`, `Some("room-model")`, or `Some("default-model")`).

### 6. **server.rs Matrix Registration Pattern** (`/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/helix-epoch/crates/gateway/src/server.rs:2665-2675`)

```rust
#[cfg(feature = "matrix")]
{
    let matrix_plugin = Arc::new(tokio::sync::RwLock::new(
        moltis_matrix::MatrixPlugin::new()
            .with_message_log(Arc::clone(&message_log))
            .with_event_sink(Arc::clone(&channel_sink)),
    ));
    registry
        .register(matrix_plugin as Arc<tokio::sync::RwLock<dyn ChannelPlugin>>)
        .await;
}
```

**All plugins follow the same pattern** (Telegram 2637–2644, MSTeams 2646–2654, Discord 2656–2663):
- Create new plugin
- Chain `.with_message_log()` and `.with_event_sink()`
- Register with channel registry
- Plugin accounts are collected from config + storage, then started concurrently (lines 2714–2794)

     3→/// Typed read-only view of common channel account config fields.
     4→///
     5→/// Each plugin's concrete config type (e.g. `TelegramAccountConfig`) implements
     6→/// this trait. The gateway and registry access typed fields instead of digging
     7→/// into raw `serde_json::Value`.
     8→///
     9→/// The store persists `Value` via `StoredChannel`. This trait is purely for
    10→/// typed read access to shared config fields.
    11→pub trait ChannelConfigView: Send + Sync + std::fmt::Debug {
    12→    /// DM user/peer allowlist.

    14→

    20→
    21→    /// Group access policy.
    22→    fn group_policy(&self) -> GroupPolicy;
    23→

    25→    fn model(&self) -> Option<&str>;
    26→
    27→    /// Provider name associated with the model.
    28→    fn model_provider(&self) -> Option<&str>;
    29→
    30→    // ── Per-channel / per-user override methods ─────────────────────────────
    31→
    32→    /// Model override for a specific channel/chat ID.
    33→    fn channel_model(&self, _channel_id: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    34→        None
    35→    }
    36→
    37→    /// Provider override for a specific channel/chat ID.

    39→        None
    40→    }
    41→
    42→    /// Model override for a specific user.
    43→    fn user_model(&self, _user_id: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    44→        None
    45→    }
    46→
    47→    /// Provider override for a specific user.
    48→    fn user_model_provider(&self, _user_id: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    49→        None
    50→    }
    51→
    52→    /// Resolve effective model: user > channel > account default.
    53→    fn resolve_model(&self, channel_id: &str, user_id: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    54→        self.user_model(user_id)
    55→            .or_else(|| self.channel_model(channel_id))
    56→            .or_else(|| self.model())
    57→    }
    58→
    59→    /// Resolve effective provider: user > channel > account default.
    60→    fn resolve_model_provider(&self, channel_id: &str, user_id: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    61→        self.user_model_provider(user_id)
    62→            .or_else(|| self.channel_model_provider(channel_id))
    63→            .or_else(|| self.model_provider())
    64→    }

  "content": "use moltis_channels::Error as ChannelError;\n\n#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]\npub enum Error {\n    #[error(\"nostr SDK error: {0}\")]\n    Sdk(#[from] nostr_sdk::client::Error),\n\n    #[error(\"nostr key error: {0}\")]\n    Key(#[from] nostr_sdk::prelude::key::Error),\n\n    #[error(\"invalid config: {0}\")]\n    Config(String),\n\n    #[error(\"relay error: {0}\")]\n    Relay(String),\n\n    #[error(\"encryption error: {0}\")]\n    Encryption(String),\n\n    #[error(\"event not found: {0}\")]\n    NotFound(String),\n}\n\nimpl Error {\n    /// Whether this error is transient and the operation may succeed on retry.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn is_retryable(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, Self::Sdk(_) | Self::Relay(_))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl From<Error> for ChannelError {\n    fn from(e: Error) -> Self {\n        match e {\n            Error::Config(msg) => ChannelError::invalid_input(msg),\n            Error::NotFound(id) => ChannelError::unavailable(format!(\"event not found: {id}\")),\n            other => ChannelError::external(\"nostr\", other),\n        }\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "content": "//! Nostr key parsing and validation.\n//!\n//! Accepts `nsec1...` (bech32) or 64-character hex secret keys.\n//! Derives public keys and normalizes `npub1...` or hex pubkeys.\n\nuse nostr_sdk::prelude::{Keys, PublicKey, SecretKey};\nuse secrecy::{ExposeSecret, Secret};\n\nuse crate::error::Error;\n\n/// Parse a secret key from either `nsec1...` bech32 or 64-char hex.\npub fn parse_secret_key(input: &Secret<String>) -> Result<SecretKey, Error> {\n    let raw = input.expose_secret();\n    SecretKey::parse(raw).map_err(|e| Error::Config(format!(\"invalid secret key: {e}\")))\n}\n\n/// Derive the full `Keys` (secret + public) from a secret key string.\npub fn derive_keys(secret: &Secret<String>) -> Result<Keys, Error> {\n    let sk = parse_secret_key(secret)?;\n    Ok(Keys::new(sk))\n}\n\n/// Parse a public key from `npub1...` bech32 or 64-char hex.\npub fn parse_pubkey(input: &str) -> Result<PublicKey, Error> {\n    PublicKey::parse(input).map_err(|e| Error::Config(format!(\"invalid pubkey '{input}': {e}\")))\n}\n\n/// Normalize a list of pubkey strings (npub1/hex) into hex-only strings.\n/// Invalid entries are logged and skipped.\npub fn normalize_pubkeys(raw: &[String]) -> Vec<PublicKey> {\n    raw.iter()\n        .filter_map(|s| match parse_pubkey(s) {\n            Ok(pk) => Some(pk),\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\"skipping invalid pubkey in allowlist: {e}\");\n                None\n            }\n        })\n        .collect()\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use secrecy::Secret;\n\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parse_hex_secret_key() {\n        // Generate a random key pair and round-trip through hex\n        let keys = Keys::generate();\n        let hex = keys.secret_key().to_secret_hex();\n        let secret = Secret::new(hex);\n        let parsed = parse_secret_key(&secret);\n        assert!(parsed.is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(\n            parsed.ok().map(|sk| sk.to_secret_hex()),\n            Some(keys.secret_key().to_secret_hex())\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parse_bech32_secret_key() {\n        let keys = Keys::generate();\n        let nsec = keys.secret_key().to_bech32();\n        let secret = Secret::new(nsec);\n        let parsed = parse_secret_key(&secret);\n        assert!(parsed.is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(\n            parsed.ok().map(|sk| sk.to_secret_hex()),\n            Some(keys.secret_key().to_secret_hex())\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn derive_keys_from_secret() {\n        let original = Keys::generate();\n        let secret = Secret::new(original.secret_key().to_secret_hex());\n        let derived = derive_keys(&secret);\n        assert!(derived.is_ok());\n        let derived = derived.unwrap_or_else(|_| unreachable!());\n        assert_eq!(derived.public_key(), original.public_key());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parse_pubkey_hex() {\n        let keys = Keys::generate();\n        let hex = keys.public_key().to_hex();\n        let parsed = parse_pubkey(&hex);\n        assert!(parsed.is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(parsed.ok(), Some(keys.public_key()));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parse_pubkey_bech32() {\n        let keys = Keys::generate();\n        let npub = keys.public_key().to_bech32();\n        let parsed = parse_pubkey(&npub);\n        assert!(parsed.is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(parsed.ok(), Some(keys.public_key()));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn invalid_secret_key_rejected() {\n        let secret = Secret::new(\"not-a-key\".to_string());\n        assert!(parse_secret_key(&secret).is_err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn invalid_pubkey_rejected() {\n        assert!(parse_pubkey(\"not-a-pubkey\").is_err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn normalize_pubkeys_skips_invalid() {\n        let keys = Keys::generate();\n        let valid = keys.public_key().to_hex();\n        let list = vec![valid.clone(), \"invalid\".to_string()];\n        let result = normalize_pubkeys(&list);\n        assert_eq!(result.len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(result[0].to_hex(), valid);\n    }\n}\n"
}

secrecy::Secret,\n    serde::{Deserialize, Serialize, ser::SerializeStruct},\n};\n\n/// NIP-01 profile metadata to publish on connect.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(default)]\npub struct NostrProfile {\n    /// Bot display name.\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub name: Option<String>,\n    /// Longer display name.\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub display_name: Option<String>,\n    /// Short bio / about text.\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub about: Option<String>,\n    /// Avatar URL (HTTPS).\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub picture: Option<String>,\n    /// NIP-05 identifier (e.g. `bot@example.com`).\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub nip05: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Configuration for a single Nostr account.\n#[derive(Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(default)]\npub struct NostrAccountConfig {\n    /// Secret key in `nsec1...` (bech32) or 64-char hex format.\n    #[serde(serialize_with = \"secret_serde::serialize_secret\")]\n    pub secret_key: Secret<String>,\n\n    /// Relay WebSocket URLs (e.g. `wss://relay.damus.io`).\n    pub relays: Vec<String>,\n\n    /// DM access policy.\n    pub dm_policy: DmPolicy,\n\n    /// Public keys allowed to send DMs (npub1/hex).\n    pub allowed_pubkeys: Vec<String>,\n\n    /// Whether this account is enabled.\n    pub enabled: bool,\n\n    /// NIP-01 profile metadata to publish on connect.\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub profile: Option<NostrProfile>,\n\n    /// Default model ID for sessions created from this account.\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub model: Option<String>,\n\n    /// Provider name associated with the model.\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub model_provider: Option<String>,\n\n    /// Enable OTP self-approval for non-allowlisted DM users.\n    pub otp_self_approval: bool,\n\n    /// Cooldown in seconds after 3 failed OTP attempts.\n    pub otp_cooldown_secs: u64,\n}\n\nimpl Default for NostrAccountConfig {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            secret_key: Secret::new(String::new()),\n            relays: default_relays(),\n            dm_policy: DmPolicy::Allowlist,\n            allowed_pubkeys: Vec::new(),\n            enabled: true,\n            profile: None,\n            model: None,\n            model_provider: None,\n            otp_self_approval: true,\n            otp_cooldown_secs: 300,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn default_relays() -> Vec<String> {\n    vec![\n        \"wss://relay.damus.io\".into(),\n        \"wss://relay.nostr.band\".into(),\n        \"wss://nos.lol\".into(),\n    ]\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Debug for NostrAccountConfig {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        f.debug_struct(\"NostrAccountConfig\")\n            .field(\"secret_key\", &\"[REDACTED]\")\n            .field(\"relays\", &self.relays)\n            .field(\"dm_policy\", &self.dm_policy)\n            .field(\"allowed_pubkeys\", &self.allowed_pubkeys)\n            .field(\"enabled\", &self.enabled)\n            .field(\"profile\", &self.profile)\n            .field(\"model\", &self.model)\n            .field(\"model_provider\", &self.model_provider)\n            .field(\"otp_self_approval\", &self.otp_self_approval)\n            .field(\"otp_cooldown_secs\", &self.otp_cooldown_secs)\n            .finish()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Wrapper that serializes secret fields as `[REDACTED]` for API responses.\npub struct RedactedConfig<'a>(pub &'a NostrAccountConfig);\n\nimpl Serialize for RedactedConfig<'_> {\n    fn serialize<S: serde::Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {\n        let c = self.0;\n        let mut s = serializer.serialize_struct(\"NostrAccountConfig\", 10)?;\n        s.serialize_field(\"secret_key\", \"[REDACTED]\")?;\n        s.serialize_field(\"relays\", &c.relays)?;\n        s.serialize_field(\"dm_policy\", &c.dm_policy)?;\n        s.serialize_field(\"allowed_pubkeys\", &c.allowed_pubkeys)?;\n        s.serialize_field(\"enabled\", &c.enabled)?;\n        s.serialize_field(\"profile\", &c.profile)?;\n        s.serialize_field(\"model\", &c.model)?;\n        s.serialize_field(\"model_provider\", &c.model_provider)?;\n        s.serialize_field(\"otp_self_approval\", &c.otp_self_approval)?;\n        s.serialize_field(\"otp_cooldown_secs\", &c.otp_cooldown_secs)?;\n        s.end()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ChannelConfigView for NostrAccountConfig {\n    fn allowlist(&self) -> &[String] {\n        &self.allowed_pubkeys\n    }\n\n    fn group_allowlist(&self) -> &[String] {\n        // Nostr DMs are always 1:1, no group concept\n        &[]\n    }\n\n    fn dm_policy(&self) -> DmPolicy {\n        self.dm_policy.clone()\n    }\n\n    fn group_policy(&self) -> GroupPolicy {\n        GroupPolicy::Disabled\n    }\n\n    fn model(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        self.model.as_deref()\n    }\n\n    fn model_provider(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        self.model_provider.as_deref()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use secrecy::Secret;\n\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn default_config_has_sensible_values() {\n        let cfg = NostrAccountConfig::default();\n        assert_eq!(cfg.dm_policy, DmPolicy::Allowlist);\n        assert_eq!(cfg.relays.len(), 3);\n        assert!(cfg.enabled);\n        assert!(cfg.otp_self_approval);\n        assert_eq!(cfg.otp_cooldown_secs, 300);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn redacted_config_hides_secret() {\n        let cfg = NostrAccountConfig {\n            secret_key: Secret::new(\"nsec1test\".into()),\n            ..Default::default()\n        };\n        let json = serde_json::to_value(RedactedConfig(&cfg));\n        assert!(json.is_ok());\n        let json = json.unwrap_or_default();\n        assert_eq!(json[\"secret_key\"], \"[REDACTED]\");\n        assert!(json[\"relays\"].is_array());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn round_trip_json() {\n        let cfg = NostrAccountConfig {\n            secret_key: Secret::new(\"deadbeef\".repeat(8)),\n            relays: vec![\"wss://test.relay\".into()],\n            dm_policy: DmPolicy::Open,\n            allowed_pubkeys: vec![\"npub1test\".into()],\n            ..Default::default()\n        };\n        let json = serde_json::to_value(&cfg);\n        assert!(json.is_ok());\n        let json = json.unwrap_or_default();\n        let parsed: Result<NostrAccountConfig, _> = serde_json::from_value(json);\n        assert!(parsed.is_ok());\n        let parsed = parsed.unwrap_or_default();\n        assert_eq!(parsed.dm_policy, DmPolicy::Open);\n        assert_eq!(parsed.relays, vec![\"wss://test.relay\"]);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn config_view_dm_only() {\n        let cfg = NostrAccountConfig {\n            model: Some(\"test-model\".into()),\n            model_provider: Some(\"test-provider\".into()),\n            ..Default::default()\n        };\n        assert_eq!(cfg.group_policy(), GroupPolicy::Disabled);\n        assert!(cfg.group_allowlist().is_empty());\n        assert_eq!(cfg.model(), Some(\"test-model\"));\n        assert_eq!(cfg.model_provider(), Some(\"test-provider\"));\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "content": "//! LRU dedup tracker for Nostr event IDs.\n//!\n//! Prevents processing the same event twice when relays replay events\n//! on reconnect. Uses a bounded HashMap with insertion-order eviction.\n\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\n\nuse nostr_sdk::prelude::EventId;\nuse time::OffsetDateTime;\n\n/// Maximum number of event IDs to track.\nconst DEFAULT_CAPACITY: usize = 100_000;\n\n/// How long an event ID is considered \"seen\" (1 hour).\nconst TTL_SECS: i64 = 3600;\n\n/// LRU-style dedup tracker keyed by Nostr event ID.\npub struct SeenTracker {\n    entries: HashMap<EventId, i64>,\n    capacity: usize,\n}\n\nimpl SeenTracker {\n    /// Create a new tracker with default capacity.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            entries: HashMap::with_capacity(1024),\n            capacity: DEFAULT_CAPACITY,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a tracker with custom capacity.\n    #[cfg(test)]\n    pub fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            entries: HashMap::with_capacity(capacity.min(1024)),\n            capacity,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns `true` if this event ID has already been seen (within TTL).\n    /// Inserts it if not yet seen.\n    pub fn check_and_insert(&mut self, id: &EventId) -> bool {\n        let now = OffsetDateTime::now_utc().unix_timestamp();\n\n        // Already seen and within TTL\n        if let Some(&ts) = self.entries.get(id) {\n            if now - ts < TTL_SECS {\n                return true;\n            }\n            // Expired — will be re-inserted below\n        }\n\n        // Evict oldest entries if at capacity\n        if self.entries.len() >= self.capacity {\n            self.evict_expired(now);\n        }\n        // If still at capacity after expiry sweep, remove ~10% oldest\n        if self.entries.len() >= self.capacity {\n            self.evict_oldest();\n        }\n\n        self.entries.insert(*id, now);\n        false\n    }\n\n    /// Remove entries older than TTL.\n    fn evict_expired(&mut self, now: i64) {\n        self.entries.retain(|_, ts| now - *ts < TTL_SECS);\n    }\n\n    /// Remove the oldest ~10% of entries by timestamp.\n    fn evict_oldest(&mut self) {\n        let to_remove = self.capacity / 10;\n        let mut by_age: Vec<(EventId, i64)> =\n            self.entries.iter().map(|(k, v)| (*k, *v)).collect();\n        by_age.sort_by_key(|(_, ts)| *ts);\n        for (id, _) in by_age.into_iter().take(to_remove) {\n            self.entries.remove(&id);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Number of tracked event IDs.\n    #[cfg(test)]\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.entries.len()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for SeenTracker {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use nostr_sdk::prelude::Keys;\n\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn random_event_id() -> EventId {\n        // Use a random key's pubkey bytes as a stand-in for event ID\n        EventId::from_byte_array(Keys::generate().public_key().to_bytes())\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn first_insert_returns_false() {\n        let mut tracker = SeenTracker::new();\n        let id = random_event_id();\n        assert!(!tracker.check_and_insert(&id));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn second_insert_returns_true() {\n        let mut tracker = SeenTracker::new();\n        let id = random_event_id();\n        assert!(!tracker.check_and_insert(&id));\n        assert!(tracker.check_and_insert(&id));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn different_ids_not_confused() {\n        let mut tracker = SeenTracker::new();\n        let id1 = random_event_id();\n        let id2 = random_event_id();\n        assert!(!tracker.check_and_insert(&id1));\n        assert!(!tracker.check_and_insert(&id2));\n        assert!(tracker.check_and_insert(&id1));\n        assert!(tracker.check_and_insert(&id2));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn capacity_eviction() {\n        let mut tracker = SeenTracker::with_capacity(10);\n        for _ in 0..20 {\n            let id = random_event_id();\n            tracker.check_and_insert(&id);\n        }\n        // Should never exceed capacity (plus small margin from eviction batching)\n        assert!(tracker.len() <= 10);\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "content": "//! DM access control for Nostr channels.\n//!\n//! Reuses `DmPolicy` from `moltis_channels::gating` and maps Nostr pubkeys\n//! to the allowlist/OTP gating model used by other channels.\n\nuse moltis_channels::gating::DmPolicy;\nuse nostr_sdk::prelude::PublicKey;\n\nuse crate::keys::normalize_pubkeys;\n\n/// Check whether a sender pubkey is authorized under the given DM policy.\n///\n/// Returns `Ok(())` if allowed, `Err(AccessDenied)` with a reason if not.\npub fn check_dm_access(\n    sender: &PublicKey,\n    policy: &DmPolicy,\n    raw_allowlist: &[String],\n) -> Result<(), AccessDenied> {\n    match policy {\n        DmPolicy::Disabled => Err(AccessDenied::Disabled),\n        DmPolicy::Open => Ok(()),\n        DmPolicy::Allowlist => {\n            let allowed = normalize_pubkeys(raw_allowlist);\n            if allowed.iter().any(|pk| pk == sender) {\n                Ok(())\n            } else {\n                Err(AccessDenied::NotAllowlisted)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Reason a DM was denied.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum AccessDenied {\n    /// DMs are globally disabled for this account.\n    Disabled,\n    /// Sender pubkey is not in the allowlist.\n    NotAllowlisted,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for AccessDenied {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Self::Disabled => write!(f, \"DMs are disabled\"),\n            Self::NotAllowlisted => write!(f, \"sender not in allowlist\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use moltis_channels::gating::DmPolicy;\n    use nostr_sdk::prelude::Keys;\n\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn open_policy_allows_anyone() {\n        let sender = Keys::generate().public_key();\n        let result = check_dm_access(&sender, &DmPolicy::Open, &[]);\n        assert!(result.is_ok());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn disabled_policy_denies_everyone() {\n        let sender = Keys::generate().public_key();\n        let result = check_dm_access(&sender, &DmPolicy::Disabled, &[]);\n        assert_eq!(result, Err(AccessDenied::Disabled));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn allowlist_policy_allows_listed() {\n        let keys = Keys::generate();\n        let allowlist = vec![keys.public_key().to_hex()];\n        let result = check_dm_access(&keys.public_key(), &DmPolicy::Allowlist, &allowlist);\n        assert!(result.is_ok());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn allowlist_policy_denies_unlisted() {\n        let sender = Keys::generate().public_key();\n        let other = Keys::generate().public_key();\n        let allowlist = vec![other.to_hex()];\n        let result = check_dm_access(&sender, &DmPolicy::Allowlist, &allowlist);\n        assert_eq!(result, Err(AccessDenied::NotAllowlisted));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn allowlist_accepts_npub_format() {\n        let keys = Keys::generate();\n        let allowlist = vec![keys.public_key().to_bech32()];\n        let result = check_dm_access(&keys.public_key(), &DmPolicy::Allowlist, &allowlist);\n        assert!(result.is_ok());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn allowlist_skips_invalid_entries() {\n        let sender = Keys::generate().public_key();\n        let allowlist = vec![\"invalid-key\".to_string()];\n        let result = check_dm_access(&sender, &DmPolicy::Allowlist, &allowlist);\n        assert_eq!(result, Err(AccessDenied::NotAllowlisted));\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "content": "//! Nostr relay subscription loop — inbound DM pipeline.\n//!\n//! Subscribes to kind:4 (NIP-04 encrypted DMs) addressed to the bot's pubkey.\n//! Events flow through dedup, self-message filtering, access control, and\n//! decryption before being dispatched to the gateway via `ChannelEventSink`.\n\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse nostr_sdk::prelude::*;\nuse time::OffsetDateTime;\nuse tokio::sync::RwLock;\nuse tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;\n\nuse crate::{\n    access::{self, AccessDenied},\n    config::NostrAccountConfig,\n    seen::SeenTracker,\n};\n\n/// Maximum plaintext message size in bytes.\nconst MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024;\n\n/// Run the relay subscription loop for a single Nostr account.\n///\n/// Subscribes to NIP-04 DMs (kind:4) targeted at `bot_pubkey` and dispatches\n/// inbound messages to the gateway. Runs until `cancel` is triggered.\npub async fn run_subscription_loop(\n    client: Client,\n    keys: Keys,\n    config: Arc<RwLock<NostrAccountConfig>>,\n    account_id: String,\n    event_sink: Arc<dyn moltis_channels::ChannelEventSink>,\n    cancel: CancellationToken,\n) {\n    let bot_pubkey = keys.public_key();\n    let since = Timestamp::from(\n        u64::try_from(OffsetDateTime::now_utc().unix_timestamp()).unwrap_or_default(),\n    );\n\n    let filter = Filter::new()\n        .kind(Kind::EncryptedDirectMessage)\n        .pubkey(bot_pubkey)\n        .since(since);\n\n    tracing::info!(\n        account_id,\n        pubkey = %bot_pubkey.to_bech32(),\n        \"starting Nostr DM subscription\"\n    );\n\n    let mut seen = SeenTracker::new();\n\n    // Subscribe and handle notifications\n    if let Err(e) = client.subscribe(vec![filter], None).await {\n        tracing::error!(account_id, \"failed to subscribe: {e}\");\n        return;\n    }\n\n    loop {\n        tokio::select! {\n            () = cancel.cancelled() => {\n                tracing::info!(account_id, \"Nostr subscription cancelled\");\n                break;\n            }\n            notification = client.notifications().recv() => {\n                match notification {\n                    Ok(RelayPoolNotification::Event { event, .. }) => {\n                        handle_event(\n                            &event,\n                            &keys,\n                            &bot_pubkey,\n                            since,\n                            &mut seen,\n                            &config,\n                            &account_id,\n                            &event_sink,\n                        ).await;\n                    }\n                    Ok(RelayPoolNotification::Shutdown) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(account_id, \"relay pool shutdown\");\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    Ok(_) => {} // RelayStatus, Message, etc.\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(account_id, \"notification channel error: {e}\");\n                        // Channel lagged — continue listening\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    tracing::info!(account_id, \"Nostr subscription loop exited\");\n}\n\n/// Process a single inbound event through the pipeline.\n#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\nasync fn handle_event(\n    event: &Event,\n    keys: &Keys,\n    bot_pubkey: &PublicKey,\n    since: Timestamp,\n    seen: &mut SeenTracker,\n    config: &Arc<RwLock<NostrAccountConfig>>,\n    account_id: &str,\n    event_sink: &Arc<dyn moltis_channels::ChannelEventSink>,\n) {\n    // 1. Skip non-DM events (belt-and-suspenders; filter should handle this)\n    if event.kind != Kind::EncryptedDirectMessage {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // 2. Dedup check\n    if seen.check_and_insert(&event.id) {\n        tracing::trace!(event_id = %event.id, \"skipping duplicate event\");\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // 3. Skip self-messages\n    if event.pubkey == *bot_pubkey {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // 4. Skip stale events (before subscription start)\n    if event.created_at < since {\n        tracing::trace!(event_id = %event.id, \"skipping stale event\");\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // 5. Access control (BEFORE decryption)\n    let cfg = config.read().await;\n    let access_result = access::check_dm_access(\n        &event.pubkey,\n        &cfg.dm_policy,\n        &cfg.allowed_pubkeys,\n    );\n\n    let sender_hex = event.pubkey.to_hex();\n\n    match &access_result {\n        Ok(()) => {}\n        Err(AccessDenied::Disabled) => {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                account_id,\n                sender = sender_hex,\n                \"DM rejected: DMs disabled\"\n            );\n            return;\n        }\n        Err(AccessDenied::NotAllowlisted) => {\n            // Emit OTP challenge event if OTP is enabled\n            if cfg.otp_self_approval {\n                event_sink\n                    .emit(moltis_channels::ChannelEvent::InboundMessage {\n                        channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n                        account_id: account_id.to_string(),\n                        peer_id: sender_hex.clone(),\n                        username: Some(event.pubkey.to_bech32()),\n                        sender_name: None,\n                        message_count: None,\n                        access_granted: false,\n                    })\n                    .await;\n                // OTP flow handled by plugin's OTP provider\n                return;\n            }\n            tracing::debug!(\n                account_id,\n                sender = sender_hex,\n                \"DM rejected: not allowlisted\"\n            );\n            return;\n        }\n    }\n    drop(cfg);\n\n    // 6. Decrypt content (NIP-04)\n    let plaintext = match nip04::decrypt(keys.secret_key(), &event.pubkey, &event.content) {\n        Ok(text) => text,\n        Err(e) => {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                account_id,\n                event_id = %event.id,\n                \"failed to decrypt DM: {e}\"\n            );\n            return;\n        }\n    };\n\n    // 7. Size validation\n    if plaintext.len() > MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES {\n        tracing::warn!(\n            account_id,\n            event_id = %event.id,\n            len = plaintext.len(),\n            \"DM exceeds size limit, truncating\"\n        );\n    }\n    let text = if plaintext.len() > MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES {\n        &plaintext[..MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES]\n    } else {\n        &plaintext\n    };\n\n    // 8. Emit inbound event for UI\n    event_sink\n        .emit(moltis_channels::ChannelEvent::InboundMessage {\n            channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n            account_id: account_id.to_string(),\n            peer_id: sender_hex.clone(),\n            username: Some(event.pubkey.to_bech32()),\n            sender_name: None,\n            message_count: None,\n            access_granted: true,\n        })\n        .await;\n\n    // 9. Dispatch to gateway chat\n    let reply_to = moltis_channels::ChannelReplyTarget {\n        channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n        account_id: account_id.to_string(),\n        chat_id: sender_hex,\n        message_id: Some(event.id.to_hex()),\n        thread_id: None,\n    };\n\n    let meta = moltis_channels::ChannelMessageMeta {\n        channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n        sender_name: None,\n        username: Some(event.pubkey.to_bech32()),\n        message_kind: Some(moltis_channels::ChannelMessageKind::Text),\n        model: None,\n        audio_filename: None,\n    };\n\n    event_sink.dispatch_to_chat(text, reply_to, meta).await;\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn max_message_size_is_reasonable() {\n        assert_eq!(MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES, 64 * 1024);\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "content": "//! Outbound message sending for Nostr channels.\n//!\n//! Implements `ChannelOutbound` and `ChannelStreamOutbound` — encrypts text\n//! with NIP-04 and publishes to connected relays.\n\nuse std::{collections::HashMap, sync::Arc};\n\nuse async_trait::async_trait;\nuse moltis_channels::{\n    ChannelOutbound, ChannelStreamOutbound, Result as ChannelResult, StreamReceiver,\n    plugin::StreamEvent,\n};\nuse moltis_common::types::ReplyPayload;\nuse nostr_sdk::prelude::*;\nuse tokio::sync::RwLock;\n\nuse crate::state::AccountState;\n\n/// Shared account state map type.\npub type AccountStateMap = Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, AccountState>>>;\n\n/// Nostr outbound adapter.\npub struct NostrOutbound {\n    pub accounts: AccountStateMap,\n}\n\nimpl NostrOutbound {\n    /// Look up account state and resolve the sender pubkey for the destination.\n    async fn resolve(\n        &self,\n        account_id: &str,\n        to: &str,\n    ) -> ChannelResult<(Client, Keys, PublicKey)> {\n        let accounts = self.accounts.read().await;\n        let state = accounts.get(account_id).ok_or_else(|| {\n            moltis_channels::Error::unavailable(format!(\"nostr account not found: {account_id}\"))\n        })?;\n        let recipient = PublicKey::parse(to).map_err(|e| {\n            moltis_channels::Error::invalid_input(format!(\"invalid recipient pubkey: {e}\"))\n        })?;\n        Ok((state.client.clone(), state.keys.clone(), recipient))\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl ChannelOutbound for NostrOutbound {\n    async fn send_text(\n        &self,\n        account_id: &str,\n        to: &str,\n        text: &str,\n        _reply_to: Option<&str>,\n    ) -> ChannelResult<()> {\n        let (client, keys, recipient) = self.resolve(account_id, to).await?;\n\n        // Encrypt with NIP-04\n        let encrypted = nip04::encrypt(keys.secret_key(), &recipient, text).map_err(|e| {\n            moltis_channels::Error::external(\n                \"nostr\",\n                crate::error::Error::Encryption(format!(\"NIP-04 encrypt failed: {e}\")),\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        // Build and publish kind:4 event\n        let tag = Tag::public_key(recipient);\n        let builder = EventBuilder::new(Kind::EncryptedDirectMessage, &encrypted).tag(tag);\n\n        client.send_event_builder(builder).await.map_err(|e| {\n            moltis_channels::Error::external(\"nostr\", crate::error::Error::Sdk(e))\n        })?;\n\n        tracing::debug!(\n            account_id,\n            to = %recipient.to_bech32(),\n            len = text.len(),\n            \"sent NIP-04 DM\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn send_media(\n        &self,\n        _account_id: &str,\n        _to: &str,\n        _payload: &ReplyPayload,\n        _reply_to: Option<&str>,\n    ) -> ChannelResult<()> {\n        // Media not yet supported on Nostr (future: NIP-94)\n        tracing::debug!(\"send_media not supported for Nostr\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl ChannelStreamOutbound for NostrOutbound {\n    async fn send_stream(\n        &self,\n        account_id: &str,\n        to: &str,\n        reply_to: Option<&str>,\n        mut stream: StreamReceiver,\n    ) -> ChannelResult<()> {\n        // Nostr doesn't support edit-in-place streaming.\n        // Collect all chunks and send as a single message.\n        let mut buffer = String::new();\n\n        while let Some(event) = stream.recv().await {\n            match event {\n                StreamEvent::Delta(chunk) => buffer.push_str(&chunk),\n                StreamEvent::Done => break,\n                StreamEvent::Error(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(account_id, \"stream error: {e}\");\n                    if buffer.is_empty() {\n                        buffer.push_str(\"[Error generating response]\");\n                    }\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        if !buffer.is_empty() {\n            self.send_text(account_id, to, &buffer, reply_to).await?;\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn is_stream_enabled(&self, _account_id: &str) -> bool {\n        // Streaming is collected and sent as final — always \"enabled\" in that sense\n        true\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Debug for NostrOutbound {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        f.debug_struct(\"NostrOutbound\").finish_non_exhaustive()\n    }\n}\n"
}

AccountStateMap,\n    outbound: NostrOutbound,\n    message_log: Option<Arc<dyn MessageLog>>,\n    event_sink: Option<Arc<dyn ChannelEventSink>>,\n}\n\nimpl NostrPlugin {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        let accounts: AccountStateMap = Arc::new(RwLock::new(HashMap::new()));\n        Self {\n            outbound: NostrOutbound {\n                accounts: Arc::clone(&accounts),\n            },\n            accounts,\n            message_log: None,\n            event_sink: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn with_message_log(mut self, log: Arc<dyn MessageLog>) -> Self {\n        self.message_log = Some(log);\n        self\n    }\n\n    pub fn with_event_sink(mut self, sink: Arc<dyn ChannelEventSink>) -> Self {\n        self.event_sink = Some(sink);\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// List pending OTP challenges for a specific account.\n    pub fn pending_otp_challenges(&self, account_id: &str) -> Vec<OtpChallengeInfo> {\n        let accounts = self.accounts.blocking_read();\n }\n\n    async fn start_account(\n        &mut self,\n        account_id: &str,\n        config: serde_json::Value,\n    ) -> ChannelResult<()> {\n        let nostr_config: NostrAccountConfig = serde_json::from_value(config).map_err(|e| {\n            moltis_channels::Error::invalid_input(format!(\"invalid nostr config: {e}\"))\n        })?;\n\n        if !nostr_config.enabled {\n account_id,\n            pubkey = %bot_keys.public_key().to_bech32(),\n            relays = ?nostr_config.relays,\n            \"starting Nostr account\"\n        );\n\n        // Build nostr-sdk client\n        let client = Client::new(bot_keys.clone());\n\n        // Add relays\n        for relay_url in &nostr_config.relays {\n            if let Err(e) = client.add_relay(relay_url).await {\n                tracing::warn!(account_id, relay = relay_url, \"failed to add relay: {e}\");\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Connect to relays\n        client.connect().await;\n\n        // Publish profile if configured\n        if let Some(ref profile) = nostr_config.profile {\n            if let Err(e) = profile::publish_profile(&client, profile).await {\n                tracing::warn!(account_id, \"failed to publish profile: {e}\");\n            }\n        }\n\n        let cancel = CancellationToken::new();\n\n        // Spawn subscription loop\n        let event_sink = self.event_sink.clone().ok_or_else(|| {\n            moltis_channels::Error::unavailable(\"event sink not configured\")\n        })?;\n\n        let loop_client = client.clone();\n        let loop_keys = bot_keys.clone();\n        let loop_config = Arc::new(RwLock::new(nostr_config.clone()));\n        let loop_account_id = account_id.to_string();\n        let loop_cancel = cancel.clone();\n        let loop_sink = Arc::clone(&event_sink);\n\n        tokio::spawn(async move {\n            bus::run_subscription_loop(\n                loop_client,\n                loop_keys,\n                loop_config,\n                loop_account_id,\n                loop_sink,\n                loop_cancel,\n            )\n            .await;\n        });\n\n        // Store account state\n        let state = AccountState {\n            client,\n            keys: bot_keys,\n            config: nostr_config,\n            cancel,\n            otp: moltis_channels::otp::OtpState::new(),\n        };\n\n        self.accounts\n            .write()\n            .await\n            .insert(account_id.to_string(), state);\n\n        tracing::info!(account_id, \"Nostr account started\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn stop_account(&mut self, account_id: &str) -> ChannelResult<()> {\n        let state = self.accounts.write().await.remove(account_id);\n        if let Some(state) = state {\n            state.cancel.cancel();\n            if let Err(e) = state.client.disconnect().await {\n outbound(&self) -> Option<&dyn ChannelOutbound> {\n        Some(&self.outbound)\n    }\n\n    fn status(&self) -> Option<&dyn ChannelStatus> {\n        Some(self)\n    }\n\n    fn has_account(&self, account_id: &str) -> bool {\n        self.accounts.blocking_read().contains_key(account_id)\n    }\n\n    fn account_ids(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        self.accounts.blocking_read().keys().cloned().collect()\n    }\n\n    fn account_config(&self, account_id: &str) -> Option<Box<dyn ChannelConfigView>> {\n        let accounts =    ) -> ChannelResult<()> {\n        let new_config: NostrAccountConfig =\n            serde_json::from_value(config).map_err(|e| {\n                moltis_channels::Error::invalid_input(format!(\"invalid nostr config: {e}\"))\n            })?;\n        let mut accounts = self.accounts.blocking_write();\n        if let Some(state) = accounts.get_mut(account_id) {\n            state.config = new_config;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn shared_outbound(&self) -> Arc<dyn ChannelOutbound> {\n        Arc::new(NostrOutbound }\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl ChannelStatus for NostrPlugin {\n    async fn probe(&self, account_id: &str) -> ChannelResult<ChannelHealthSnapshot> {\n        let accounts =     94→        })?;
    95→
    96→        tracing::info!(

   125→        // Spawn subscription loop

   129→

  "content": "//! LRU dedup tracker for Nostr event IDs.\n//!\n//! Prevents processing the same event twice when relays replay events\n//! on reconnect. Uses a bounded HashMap with insertion-order eviction.\n\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\n\nuse nostr_sdk::prelude::EventId;\n\n/// Maximum number of event IDs to track.\nconst DEFAULT_CAPACITY: usize = 100_000;\n\n/// How long an event ID is considered \"seen\" (1 hour).\nconst TTL_SECS: i64 = 3600;\n\n/// LRU-style dedup tracker keyed by Nostr event ID.\npub struct SeenTracker {\n    entries: HashMap<EventId, i64>,\n    capacity: usize,\n}\n\nfn now_unix() -> i64 {\n    ::time::OffsetDateTime::now_utc().unix_timestamp()\n}\n\nimpl SeenTracker {\n    /// Create a new tracker with default capacity.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            entries: HashMap::with_capacity(1024),\n            capacity: DEFAULT_CAPACITY,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a tracker with custom capacity.\n    #[cfg(test)]\n    pub fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            entries: HashMap::with_capacity(capacity.min(1024)),\n            capacity,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns `true` if this event ID has already been seen (within TTL).\n    /// Inserts it if not yet seen.\n    pub fn check_and_insert(&mut self, id: &EventId) -> bool {\n        let now = now_unix();\n\n        // Already seen and within TTL\n        if let Some(&ts) = self.entries.get(id) {\n            if now - ts < TTL_SECS {\n                return true;\n            }\n            // Expired — will be re-inserted below\n        }\n\n        // Evict oldest entries if at capacity\n        if self.entries.len() >= self.capacity {\n            self.evict_expired(now);\n        }\n        // If still at capacity after expiry sweep, remove ~10% oldest\n        if self.entries.len() >= self.capacity {\n            self.evict_oldest();\n        }\n\n        self.entries.insert(*id, now);\n        false\n    }\n\n    /// Remove entries older than TTL.\n    fn evict_expired(&mut self, now: i64) {\n        self.entries.retain(|_, ts| now - *ts < TTL_SECS);\n    }\n\n    /// Remove the oldest ~10% of entries by timestamp.\n    fn evict_oldest(&mut self) {\n        let to_remove = self.capacity / 10;\n        let mut by_age: Vec<(EventId, i64)> =\n            self.entries.iter().map(|(k, v)| (*k, *v)).collect();\n        by_age.sort_by_key(|(_, ts)| *ts);\n        for (id, _) in by_age.into_iter().take(to_remove) {\n            self.entries.remove(&id);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Number of tracked event IDs.\n    #[cfg(test)]\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.entries.len()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for SeenTracker {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use nostr_sdk::prelude::Keys;\n\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn random_event_id() -> EventId {\n        EventId::from_byte_array(Keys::generate().public_key().to_bytes())\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn first_insert_returns_false() {\n        let mut tracker = SeenTracker::new();\n        let id = random_event_id();\n        assert!(!tracker.check_and_insert(&id));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn second_insert_returns_true() {\n        let mut tracker = SeenTracker::new();\n        let id = random_event_id();\n        assert!(!tracker.check_and_insert(&id));\n        assert!(tracker.check_and_insert(&id));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn different_ids_not_confused() {\n        let mut tracker = SeenTracker::new();\n        let id1 = random_event_id();\n        let id2 = random_event_id();\n        assert!(!tracker.check_and_insert(&id1));\n        assert!(!tracker.check_and_insert(&id2));\n        assert!(tracker.check_and_insert(&id1));\n        assert!(tracker.check_and_insert(&id2));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn capacity_eviction() {\n        let mut tracker = SeenTracker::with_capacity(10);\n        for _ in 0..20 {\n            let id = random_event_id();\n            tracker.check_and_insert(&id);\n        }\n        // Should never exceed capacity (plus small margin from eviction batching)\n        assert!(tracker.len() <= 10);\n    }\n}\n"
}

Events flow through dedup, self-message filtering, access control, and\n//! decryption before being dispatched to the gateway via `ChannelEventSink`.\n\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse nostr_sdk::prelude::*;\nuse tokio::sync::RwLock;\nuse tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;\n\nuse crate::{\n    access::{self, AccessDenied},\n    config::NostrAccountConfig,\n    seen::SeenTracker,\n};\n\n/// Maximum plaintext message size in bytes.\nconst MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024;\n\n/// Run the relay subscription loop for a single Nostr account.\n///\n/// Subscribes to NIP-04 DMs (kind:4) targeted at `bot_pubkey` and dispatches\n/// inbound messages to the gateway. Runs until `cancel` is triggered.\npub async fn run_subscription_loop(\n    client: Client,\n    keys: Keys,\n    config: Arc<RwLock<NostrAccountConfig>>,\n    account_id: String,\n    event_sink: Arc<dyn moltis_channels::ChannelEventSink>,\n    cancel: CancellationToken,\n) {\n    let bot_pubkey = keys.public_key();\n    let now_secs =\n        u64::try_from(::time::OffsetDateTime::now_utc().unix_timestamp()).unwrap_or_default();\n    let since = Timestamp::from(now_secs);\n\n    let filter = Filter::new()\n        .kind(Kind::EncryptedDirectMessage)\n        .pubkey(bot_pubkey)\n        .since(since);\n\n    tracing::info!(\n        account_id,\n        pubkey = %bot_pubkey.to_bech32(),\n        \"starting Nostr DM subscription\"\n    );\n\n    let mut seen = SeenTracker::new();\n\n    // Subscribe and handle notifications\n    if let Err(e) = client.subscribe(vec![filter], None).await {\n        tracing::error!(account_id, \"failed to subscribe: {e}\");\n        return;\n    }\n\n    loop {\n        tokio::select! {\n            () = cancel.cancelled() => {\n                tracing::info!(account_id, \"Nostr subscription cancelled\");\n                break;\n            }\n            notification = client.notifications().recv() => {\n                match notification {\n                    Ok(RelayPoolNotification::Event { event, .. }) => {\n                        handle_event(\n                            &event,\n                            &keys,\n                            &bot_pubkey,\n                            since,\n                            &mut seen,\n                            &config,\n                            &account_id,\n                            &event_sink,\n                        ).await;\n                    }\n                    Ok(RelayPoolNotification::Shutdown) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(account_id, \"relay pool shutdown\");\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    Ok(_) => {} // RelayStatus, Message, etc.\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(account_id, \"notification channel error: {e}\");\n                        // Channel lagged — continue listening\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    tracing::info!(account_id, \"Nostr subscription loop exited\");\n}\n\n/// Process a single inbound event through the pipeline.\n#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\nasync fn handle_event(\n    event: &Event,\n    keys: &Keys,\n    bot_pubkey: &PublicKey,\n    since: Timestamp,\n    seen: &mut SeenTracker,\n    config: &Arc<RwLock<NostrAccountConfig>>,\n    account_id: &str,\n    event_sink: &Arc<dyn moltis_channels::ChannelEventSink>,\n) {\n    // 1. Skip non-DM events (belt-and-suspenders; filter should handle this)\n    if event.kind != Kind::EncryptedDirectMessage {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // 2. Dedup check\n    if seen.check_and_insert(&event.id) {\n        tracing::trace!(event_id = %event.id, \"skipping duplicate event\");\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // 3. Skip self-messages\n    if event.pubkey == *bot_pubkey {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // 4. Skip stale events (before subscription start)\n    if event.created_at < since {\n        tracing::trace!(event_id = %event.id, \"skipping stale event\");\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // 5. Access control (BEFORE decryption)\n    let cfg = config.read().await;\n    let access_result = access::check_dm_access(\n        &event.pubkey,\n        &cfg.dm_policy,\n        &cfg.allowed_pubkeys,\n    );\n\n    let sender_hex = event.pubkey.to_hex();\n\n    match &access_result {\n        Ok(()) => {}\n        Err(AccessDenied::Disabled) => {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                account_id,\n                sender = sender_hex,\n                \"DM rejected: DMs disabled\"\n            );\n            return;\n        }\n        Err(AccessDenied::NotAllowlisted) => {\n            // Emit OTP challenge event if OTP is enabled\n            if cfg.otp_self_approval {\n                event_sink\n                    .emit(moltis_channels::ChannelEvent::InboundMessage {\n                        channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n                        account_id: account_id.to_string(),\n                        peer_id: sender_hex.clone(),\n                        username: Some(event.pubkey.to_bech32()),\n                        sender_name: None,\n                        message_count: None,\n                        access_granted: false,\n                    })\n                    .await;\n                // OTP flow handled by plugin's OTP provider\n                return;\n            }\n            tracing::debug!(\n                account_id,\n                sender = sender_hex,\n                \"DM rejected: not allowlisted\"\n            );\n            return;\n        }\n    }\n    drop(cfg);\n\n    // 6. Decrypt content (NIP-04)\n    let plaintext = match nip04::decrypt(keys.secret_key(), &event.pubkey, &event.content) {\n        Ok(text) => text,\n        Err(e) => {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                account_id,\n                event_id = %event.id,\n                \"failed to decrypt DM: {e}\"\n            );\n            return;\n        }\n    };\n\n    // 7. Size validation\n    let text = if plaintext.len() > MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES {\n        tracing::warn!(\n            account_id,\n            event_id = %event.id,\n            len = plaintext.len(),\n            \"DM exceeds size limit, truncating\"\n        );\n        &plaintext[..MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES]\n    } else {\n        &plaintext\n    };\n\n    // 8. Emit inbound event for UI\n    event_sink\n        .emit(moltis_channels::ChannelEvent::InboundMessage {\n            channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n            account_id: account_id.to_string(),\n            peer_id: sender_hex.clone(),\n            username: Some(event.pubkey.to_bech32()),\n            sender_name: None,\n            message_count: None,\n            access_granted: true,\n        })\n        .await;\n\n    // 9. Dispatch to gateway chat\n    let reply_to = moltis_channels::ChannelReplyTarget {\n        channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n        account_id: account_id.to_string(),\n        chat_id: sender_hex,\n        message_id: Some(event.id.to_hex()),\n        thread_id: None,\n    };\n\n    let meta = moltis_channels::ChannelMessageMeta {\n        channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n        sender_name: None,\n        username: Some(event.pubkey.to_bech32()),\n        message_kind: Some(moltis_channels::ChannelMessageKind::Text),\n        model: None,\n        audio_filename: None,\n    };\n\n    event_sink.dispatch_to_chat(text, reply_to, meta).await;\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn max_message_size_is_reasonable() {\n        assert_eq!(MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES, 64 * 1024);\n    }\n}\n"
}

```
pub enum RelayPoolNotification {
    /// Received a new [`Event`] from a relay.
    ///
    /// This notification is sent only the **first time** the [`Event`] is seen.
    /// Events sent by this client are not included.
    /// This is useful when you only need to process new incoming events
    /// and avoid handling the same events multiple times.
    ///
    /// If you require notifications for all messages, including previously sent or received events,
    /// consider using the [`RelayPoolNotification::Message`] variant instead.
    Event {
        /// The URL of the relay from which the event was received.
        relay_url: RelayUrl,
        /// Subscription ID
        subscription_id: SubscriptionId,
        /// The received event.
        event: Box<Event>,
    },
    /// Received a [`RelayMessage`].
    ///
    /// This notification is sent **every time** a [`RelayMessage`] is received,
    /// regardless of whether it has been received before.
    ///
    /// May includes messages wrapping events that were sent by this client.
    Message {
        /// The URL of the relay from which the message was received.
        relay_url: RelayUrl,
        /// The received relay message.
        message: RelayMessage<'static>,
    },
    /// Shutdown
    ///
    /// This notification variant is sent after [`RelayPool::shutdown`] method is called and all connections have been closed.
    Shutdown,
}
