  "content": "//! Nostr relay subscription loop — inbound DM pipeline.\n//!\n//! Subscribes to kind:4 (NIP-04 encrypted DMs) addressed to the bot's pubkey.\n//! Events flow through dedup, self-message filtering, access control, and\n//! decryption before being dispatched to the gateway via `ChannelEventSink`.\n\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse nostr_sdk::prelude::*;\nuse tokio::sync::RwLock;\nuse tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;\n\nuse crate::{\n    access::{self, AccessDenied},\n    config::NostrAccountConfig,\n    seen::SeenTracker,\n};\n\n/// Maximum plaintext message size in bytes.\nconst MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024;\n\n/// Run the relay subscription loop for a single Nostr account.\n///\n/// Subscribes to NIP-04 DMs (kind:4) targeted at `bot_pubkey` and dispatches\n/// inbound messages to the gateway. Runs until `cancel` is triggered.\npub async fn run_subscription_loop(\n    client: Client,\n    keys: Keys,\n    config: Arc<RwLock<NostrAccountConfig>>,\n    account_id: String,\n    event_sink: Arc<dyn moltis_channels::ChannelEventSink>,\n    cancel: CancellationToken,\n) {\n    let bot_pubkey = keys.public_key();\n    let now_secs =\n        u64::try_from(::time::OffsetDateTime::now_utc().unix_timestamp()).unwrap_or_default();\n    let since = Timestamp::from(now_secs);\n\n    let filter = Filter::new()\n        .kind(Kind::EncryptedDirectMessage)\n        .pubkey(bot_pubkey)\n        .since(since);\n\n    let npub = bot_pubkey.to_bech32().unwrap_or_else(|_| bot_pubkey.to_hex());\n    tracing::info!(\n        account_id,\n        pubkey = %npub,\n        \"starting Nostr DM subscription\"\n    );\n\n    let mut seen = SeenTracker::new();\n\n    // Subscribe (single filter)\n    if let Err(e) = client.subscribe(filter, None).await {\n        tracing::error!(account_id, \"failed to subscribe: {e}\");\n        return;\n    }\n\n    loop {\n        tokio::select! {\n            () = cancel.cancelled() => {\n                tracing::info!(account_id, \"Nostr subscription cancelled\");\n                break;\n            }\n            notification = client.notifications().recv() => {\n                match notification {\n                    Ok(RelayPoolNotification::Event { event, .. }) => {\n                        handle_event(\n                            &event,\n                            &keys,\n                            &bot_pubkey,\n                            since,\n                            &mut seen,\n                            &config,\n                            &account_id,\n                            &event_sink,\n                        ).await;\n                    }\n                    Ok(RelayPoolNotification::Shutdown) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(account_id, \"relay pool shutdown\");\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    Ok(_) => {} // Message, etc.\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(account_id, \"notification channel error: {e}\");\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    tracing::info!(account_id, \"Nostr subscription loop exited\");\n}\n\n/// Process a single inbound event through the pipeline.\n#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\nasync fn handle_event(\n    event: &Event,\n    keys: &Keys,\n    bot_pubkey: &PublicKey,\n    since: Timestamp,\n    seen: &mut SeenTracker,\n    config: &Arc<RwLock<NostrAccountConfig>>,\n    account_id: &str,\n    event_sink: &Arc<dyn moltis_channels::ChannelEventSink>,\n) {\n    // 1. Skip non-DM events\n    if event.kind != Kind::EncryptedDirectMessage {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // 2. Dedup check\n    if seen.check_and_insert(&event.id) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // 3. Skip self-messages\n    if event.pubkey == *bot_pubkey {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // 4. Skip stale events\n    if event.created_at < since {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // 5. Access control (BEFORE decryption)\n    let cfg = config.read().await;\n    let access_result =\n        access::check_dm_access(&event.pubkey, &cfg.dm_policy, &cfg.allowed_pubkeys);\n\n    let sender_hex = event.pubkey.to_hex();\n    let sender_npub = event\n        .pubkey\n        .to_bech32()\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| sender_hex.clone());\n\n    match &access_result {\n        Ok(()) => {}\n        Err(AccessDenied::Disabled) => {\n            tracing::debug!(account_id, sender = sender_hex, \"DM rejected: disabled\");\n            return;\n        }\n        Err(AccessDenied::NotAllowlisted) => {\n            if cfg.otp_self_approval {\n                event_sink\n                    .emit(moltis_channels::ChannelEvent::InboundMessage {\n                        channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n                        account_id: account_id.to_string(),\n                        peer_id: sender_hex.clone(),\n                        username: Some(sender_npub.clone()),\n                        sender_name: None,\n                        message_count: None,\n                        access_granted: false,\n                    })\n                    .await;\n                return;\n            }\n            tracing::debug!(account_id, sender = sender_hex, \"DM rejected: not allowlisted\");\n            return;\n        }\n    }\n    drop(cfg);\n\n    // 6. Decrypt content (NIP-04)\n    let plaintext = match nip04::decrypt(keys.secret_key(), &event.pubkey, &event.content) {\n        Ok(text) => text,\n        Err(e) => {\n            tracing::warn!(account_id, event_id = %event.id, \"decrypt failed: {e}\");\n            return;\n        }\n    };\n\n    // 7. Size validation\n    let text = if plaintext.len() > MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES {\n        tracing::warn!(account_id, len = plaintext.len(), \"DM exceeds size limit\");\n        &plaintext[..MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES]\n    } else {\n        &plaintext\n    };\n\n    // 8. Emit inbound event\n    event_sink\n        .emit(moltis_channels::ChannelEvent::InboundMessage {\n            channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n            account_id: account_id.to_string(),\n            peer_id: sender_hex.clone(),\n            username: Some(sender_npub.clone()),\n            sender_name: None,\n            message_count: None,\n            access_granted: true,\n        })\n        .await;\n\n    // 9. Dispatch to gateway\n    let reply_to = moltis_channels::ChannelReplyTarget {\n        channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n        account_id: account_id.to_string(),\n        chat_id: sender_hex,\n        message_id: Some(event.id.to_hex()),\n        thread_id: None,\n    };\n\n    let meta = moltis_channels::ChannelMessageMeta {\n        channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n        sender_name: None,\n        username: Some(sender_npub),\n        message_kind: Some(moltis_channels::ChannelMessageKind::Text),\n        model: None,\n        audio_filename: None,\n    };\n\n    event_sink.dispatch_to_chat(text, reply_to, meta).await;\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn max_message_size_is_reasonable() {\n        assert_eq!(MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES, 64 * 1024);\n    }\n}\n"

> AGENT

OK so `SecretKey::to_bech32()` returns `Result<String, Infallible>`, and `PublicKey::to_bech32()` returns `Result<String, Infallible>` too — so `Infallible` error. That's what's causing the `serde_json` issue — `Infallible` doesn't implement `Serialize`. The fix in `keys.rs` tests is to call `.unwrap_or_default()` or convert to string first. Let me fix the tests:

  "content": "//! Nostr key parsing and validation.\n//!\n//! Accepts `nsec1...` (bech32) or 64-character hex secret keys.\n//! Derives public keys and normalizes `npub1...` or hex pubkeys.\n\nuse nostr_sdk::prelude::{Keys, PublicKey, SecretKey, ToBech32};\nuse secrecy::{ExposeSecret, Secret};\n\nuse crate::error::Error;\n\n/// Parse a secret key from either `nsec1...` bech32 or 64-char hex.\npub fn parse_secret_key(input: &Secret<String>) -> Result<SecretKey, Error> {\n    let raw = input.expose_secret();\n    SecretKey::parse(raw).map_err(|e| Error::Config(format!(\"invalid secret key: {e}\")))\n}\n\n/// Derive the full `Keys` (secret + public) from a secret key string.\npub fn derive_keys(secret: &Secret<String>) -> Result<Keys, Error> {\n    let sk = parse_secret_key(secret)?;\n    Ok(Keys::new(sk))\n}\n\n/// Parse a public key from `npub1...` bech32 or 64-char hex.\npub fn parse_pubkey(input: &str) -> Result<PublicKey, Error> {\n    PublicKey::parse(input).map_err(|e| Error::Config(format!(\"invalid pubkey '{input}': {e}\")))\n}\n\n/// Normalize a list of pubkey strings (npub1/hex) into parsed `PublicKey`s.\n/// Invalid entries are logged and skipped.\npub fn normalize_pubkeys(raw: &[String]) -> Vec<PublicKey> {\n    raw.iter()\n        .filter_map(|s| match parse_pubkey(s) {\n            Ok(pk) => Some(pk),\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\"skipping invalid pubkey in allowlist: {e}\");\n                None\n            }\n        })\n        .collect()\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use secrecy::Secret;\n\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parse_hex_secret_key() {\n        let keys = Keys::generate();\n        let hex = keys.secret_key().to_secret_hex();\n        let secret = Secret::new(hex);\n        let parsed = parse_secret_key(&secret);\n        assert!(parsed.is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(\n            parsed.ok().map(|sk| sk.to_secret_hex()),\n            Some(keys.secret_key().to_secret_hex())\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parse_bech32_secret_key() {\n        let keys = Keys::generate();\n        // to_bech32() returns Result<String, Infallible>\n        let nsec = keys.secret_key().to_bech32().unwrap_or_default();\n        let secret = Secret::new(nsec);\n        let parsed = parse_secret_key(&secret);\n        assert!(parsed.is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(\n            parsed.ok().map(|sk| sk.to_secret_hex()),\n            Some(keys.secret_key().to_secret_hex())\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn derive_keys_from_secret() {\n        let original = Keys::generate();\n        let secret = Secret::new(original.secret_key().to_secret_hex());\n        let derived = derive_keys(&secret);\n        assert!(derived.is_ok());\n        let derived = derived.unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!(\"derive_keys failed: {e}\"));\n        assert_eq!(derived.public_key(), original.public_key());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parse_pubkey_hex() {\n        let keys = Keys::generate();\n        let hex = keys.public_key().to_hex();\n        let parsed = parse_pubkey(&hex);\n        assert!(parsed.is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(parsed.ok(), Some(keys.public_key()));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parse_pubkey_bech32() {\n        let keys = Keys::generate();\n        let npub = keys.public_key().to_bech32().unwrap_or_default();\n        let parsed = parse_pubkey(&npub);\n        assert!(parsed.is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(parsed.ok(), Some(keys.public_key()));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn invalid_secret_key_rejected() {\n        let secret = Secret::new(\"not-a-key\".to_string());\n        assert!(parse_secret_key(&secret).is_err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn invalid_pubkey_rejected() {\n        assert!(parse_pubkey(\"not-a-pubkey\").is_err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn normalize_pubkeys_skips_invalid() {\n        let keys = Keys::generate();\n        let valid = keys.public_key().to_hex();\n        let list = vec![valid.clone(), \"invalid\".to_string()];\n        let result = normalize_pubkeys(&list);\n        assert_eq!(result.len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(result[0].to_hex(), valid);\n    }\n}\n"
}

NIP-01 profile metadata publishing.\n\nuse nostr_sdk::prelude::{Client, Metadata, Url};\n\nuse crate::{config::NostrProfile, error::Error};\n\n/// Publish NIP-01 profile metadata (kind:0) for the bot identity.\npub async fn publish_profile(client: &Client, profile: &NostrProfile) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    let mut metadata = Metadata::new();\n\n    if let Some(name) = &profile.name {\n        metadata = metadata.name(name);\n    }\n    if let Some(display_name) = &profile.display_name {\n        metadata = metadata.display_name(display_name);\n    }\n    if let Some(about) = &profile.about {\n        metadata = metadata.about(about);\n    }\n    if let Some(picture) = &profile.picture {\n        let url = Url::parse(picture)\n            .map_err(|e| Error::Config(format!(\"invalid profile picture URL: {e}\")))?;\n        metadata = metadata.picture(url);\n    }\n    if let Some(nip05) = &profile.nip05 {\n        metadata = metadata.nip05(nip05);\n    }\n\n    client\n        .set_metadata(&metadata)\n        .await\n        .map_err(Error::Sdk)?;\n\n    tracing::info!(\"published NIP-01 profile metadata\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n"
}

## Nostr DM Channel — Implementation Complete

### New crate: `crates/nostr/` (12 files, ~1700 LOC)

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `lib.rs` | Module exports, re-exports `NostrPlugin` |
| `plugin.rs` | `ChannelPlugin` impl — lifecycle, registry, OTP provider |
| `config.rs` | `NostrAccountConfig` struct, `RedactedConfig`, `ChannelConfigView` impl |
| `bus.rs` | Relay subscription loop — dedup, access control, NIP-04 decrypt, dispatch |
| `outbound.rs` | `ChannelOutbound` + `ChannelStreamOutbound` — NIP-04 encrypt + publish |
| `access.rs` | DM policy enforcement (open/allowlist/disabled) by pubkey |
| `keys.rs` | nsec1/hex secret key parsing, pubkey derivation, normalization |
| `seen.rs` | LRU dedup tracker for event IDs (100K capacity, 1h TTL) |
| `state.rs` | Per-account runtime state (client, keys, config, OTP) |
| `profile.rs` | NIP-01 profile metadata publishing (kind:0) |
| `error.rs` | `NostrError` with retryability classification |

### Modified files (13 files)

- **`ChannelType::Nostr`** variant added to `crates/channels/src/plugin.rs` with all match arms
- **Feature flag chain**: `crates/cli` → `crates/httpd` → `crates/gateway` → `crates/nostr` (default-on)
- **Config schema**: `nostr` field in `ChannelsConfig`, validation, template section
- **Gateway registration**: `#[cfg(feature = "nostr")]` block in `server.rs`

### Tests: 23 unit tests passing
- Key parsing (hex, bech32, invalid)
- Access control (open, disabled, allowlist, npub format, invalid entries)
- Config (defaults, redacted output, round-trip, config view)
- Seen tracker (insert, dedup, capacity eviction)

- **moltis-afy**: Web UI add/edit flow
- **moltis-66v**: E2E tests and documentation

## Web UI Channel Configuration Patterns - Comprehensive Findings

### 1. **Main Channel Page Structure** (`page-channels.js`)

**File Location:** `/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/helix-epoch/crates/web/src/assets/js/page-channels.js` (2,239 lines)

**Key Components:**
- **Signal-based state management** (lines 37-63):
  - `channels` — array of configured channels
  - `activeTab` — "channels" or "senders" tab
  - `showAddTelegram`, `showAddTeams`, `showAddDiscord`, `showAddSlack`, `showAddMatrix`, `showAddWhatsApp` — modal visibility
  - `editingChannel` — channel being edited
  - `sendersAccount`, `senders` — sender list state
  - WhatsApp pairing: `waQrData`, `waQrSvg`, `waPairingAccountId`, `waPairingError`

**Channel Type System:**
- `channelType(type)` (lines 65-67): Normalizes type to string, defaults to "telegram"
- `channelLabel(type)` (lines 69-77): Maps type to display label (Microsoft Teams, Discord, WhatsApp, Slack, Matrix, Telegram)
- `channelDescriptor(type)` (lines 79-82): Fetches channel capabilities from GON (server-injected data)
- `MODE_LABELS` (lines 84-90): Maps inbound modes to labels (Send only, Polling, Gateway, Socket Mode, Webhook)
- `MODE_HINTS` (lines 92-98): User guidance for each mode

### 2. **Shared Channel Form Components**

#### **AllowlistInput** (lines 595-641)
```javascript
function AllowlistInput({ value, onChange, preserveAt })
```
- Tag-based input component for allowlist entries
- Props:
  - `value` — array of tags
  - `onChange` — callback with updated array
  - `preserveAt` — boolean to keep @ prefix (for Matrix)
- **Behavior:** Enter or comma-separated items, backspace removes last tag
- **Styling:** Tailwind (`flex flex-wrap items-center gap-1.5 rounded border px-2 py-1.5`)
- **Display:** Tags rendered as colored badges with × remove button

#### **SharedChannelFields** (lines 644-674)
Renders fields common to most channels (Telegram, Teams, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp):
- **DM Policy** select: "allowlist", "open", "disabled"
- **Group Mention Mode** select: "mention" (must @mention), "always", "none"
- **Default Model** — ModelSelect component
- **DM Allowlist** — AllowlistInput component

#### **AdvancedConfigPatchField** (lines 288-315)
```javascript
function AdvancedConfigPatchField({ value, onInput, currentConfig = null })
```
- Collapsible `<details>` section
- Shows current stored config (read-only) if provided
- Textarea for JSON patch input
- Placeholder: `'{"reply_to_message": true}'`

#### **ConnectionModeHint** (lines 100-109)
```javascript
function ConnectionModeHint({ type })
```
- Displays badge + hint text for channel's inbound mode
- Uses `channelDescriptor()` to fetch capabilities
- Shows appropriate mode label and explanation

### 3. **Modal Forms by Channel Type**

#### **AddTelegramModal** (lines 677-771)
**Fields:**
- Bot username (text input, data-field="accountId")
- Bot Token (password input, data-field="credential")
- Shared fields via `<SharedChannelFields>`
- Advanced config patch

**Submission:**
- Validates via `validateChannelFields("telegram", accountId, credential)`
- Config built with: `token`, `dm_policy`, `mention_mode`, `allowlist`, `model`, `model_provider`

#### **AddMatrixModal** (lines 1313-1563)
**Complex form with authentication branching:**
- Homeserver URL (required, default: https://matrix.org)
- **Authentication mode selector:**

- Default Model
- **Two allowlists:**

  - Room Allowlist (room IDs or aliases, preserveAt=true)
- Advanced config patch

**Guidance elements:**
- Encrypted chat guidance (emerald box, lines 1422-1425)

### 4. **Edit Channel Modal** (lines 1735-2099)

**Structure:**
- One modal handles editing all channel types
- Type detection: `chType = channelType(ch.type)` with boolean flags: `isTeams`, `isDiscord`, `isWhatsApp`, `isTelegram`, `isMatrix`
- Displays channel name and account ID at top

**State signals per channel (set via useEffect):**
- Common: `editModel`, `allowlistItems`, `editCredential`, `editAdvancedConfigPatch`
- Teams-specific: `editWebhookSecret`, `editStreamMode`, `editReplyStyle`, `editWelcomeCard`, `editBotName`
- Matrix-specific: `editMatrixAuthMode`, `editMatrixDeviceDisplayName`, `editMatrixOwnershipMode`, `editMatrixOtpSelfApproval`, `editMatrixOtpCooldown`
- Matrix room allowlist: `roomAllowlistItems`

**Update workflow:**
- `buildUpdateConfig(form)` — assembles config based on channel type
- `addChannelCredentials()` — type-specific credential handling
- `addModelToConfig()` — adds model if selected
- RPC call: `channels.update({ type, account_id, config })`

### 6. **Validation Utilities** (`channel-utils.js`)

**Main validation function:**
```javascript
validateChannelFields(type, accountId, credential, options = {})
```
- Returns `{ valid: true }` or `{ valid: false, error: string }`
- Type-specific checks:
  - **telegram**: requires accountId + credential
  - **msteams**: requires accountId + "App password"
  - **matrix**: requires accountId + credential + userId (if password mode)
- Helper functions:
  - `matrixAuthModeGuidance(authMode)` — guidance based on auth mode
  - `deriveMatrixAccountId({ userId, homeserver })` — auto-generates account ID
  - `normalizeMatrixAuthMode(authMode)` — normalizes to "password" or "access_token"
  - `normalizeMatrixOwnershipMode(mode)` — normalizes to "moltis_owned" or "user_managed"
  - `parseChannelConfigPatch(text)` — validates JSON patch
  - `generateWebhookSecretHex()` — creates 48-hex-char secret for Teams
  - `buildTeamsEndpoint(baseUrl, accountId, webhookSecret)` — generates full endpoint URL

### 9. **RPC Endpoints Used**

**Channel management:**
- `channels.add(type, account_id, config)` — add new channel
- `channels.status()` — fetch all channels + status
- `channels.update(type, account_id, config)` — update channel config
- `channels.remove(type, account_id)` — delete channel
- `channels.retry_ownership(type, account_id)` — retry Matrix ownership setup

**Sender management:**
- `channels.senders.list(type, account_id)` — list senders for channel
- `channels.senders.approve(type, account_id, identifier)` — allow sender
- `channels.senders.deny(type, account_id, identifier)` — block sender

**Event subscription:**
- `onEvent("channel", callback)` — listens to channel WebSocket events
  - Event types: `pairing_complete`, `account_disabled`, `inbound_message`, `otp_challenge`, `otp_resolved`

### 10. **E2E Test Pattern** (from `settings-nav.spec.js`, lines 42-96)

**Mock helper for channels testing:**
```javascript
async function mockChannelsStatus(page, { channels, senders = [], allowRetryOwnership = false, label })
```
- Intercepts RPC calls (`channels.status`, `channels.senders.list`, `channels.retry_ownership`)
- Injects mock responses
- Useful for testing UI without real backend

**Test structure:**
- `const { expect, test } = require("../base-test")`
- `const { expectPageContentMounted, navigateAndWait, waitForWsConnected, watchPageErrors } = require("../helpers")`
- Helpers check page readiness, navigation success, WS connection, JS errors

### 11. **Data Structure Examples**

**Channel object (from fetchChannelStatus):**
```javascript
{
  type: "telegram" | "matrix" | "msteams" | "discord" | "whatsapp" | "slack",
  account_id: string,
  name: string,
  status: "connected" | string,
  details: string,
  sessions: [{ label, key, active, messageCount }, ...],
  config: {
    // common
    dm_policy: "allowlist" | "open" | "disabled",
    mention_mode: "mention" | "always" | "none",
    allowlist: [string, ...],
    model: string,
    model_provider: string,
    // telegram
    token: string,
    // matrix
    homeserver: string,
    user_id: string,
    password: string,
    access_token: string,
    device_display_name: string,
    ownership_mode: "moltis_owned" | "user_managed",
    user_allowlist: [string, ...],
    room_allowlist: [string, ...],
    room_policy: "allowlist" | "open" | "disabled",
    auto_join: "always" | "allowlist" | "off",
    otp_self_approval: boolean,
    otp_cooldown_secs: number,
    // teams
    app_id: string,
    app_password: string,
    webhook_secret: string,
    stream_mode: string,
    reply_style: string,
    welcome_card: boolean,
    bot_name: string,
  },
  extra: {
    matrix: {
      user_id: string,
      device_id: string,
      device_display_name: string,
      device_verified_by_owner: boolean,
      cross_signing_complete: boolean,
      recovery_state: string,
      verification_state: string,
      pending_verifications: [string, ...],
      ownership_mode: string,
      auth_mode: string,
      ownership_error: string,
    }
  }
}
```

**Sender object:**
```javascript
{
  peer_id: string,
  username: string,
  sender: string,
  last_seen_ms: number,
  message_count: number,
  allowed: boolean,
}
```

### 12. **Key Patterns for Adding New Channels**

1. **Create AddXxxModal component** with:
   - State signals for form fields
   - Validation function call (`validateChannelFields`)
   - Advanced config patch parsing
   - Form submission → `addChannel(type, accountId, config)`

2. **Export i18n strings** in `locales/en/channels.js`

3. **Add type to utilities**:
   - `channelLabel()` mapping
   - `channelType()` if special normalization needed

4. **Render modal in ChannelsPage**:
   - Add `show` signal
   - Add button in `ConnectButtons` component
   - Include `<${AddXxxModal} />` in ChannelsPage

5. **Edit support in EditChannelModal**:
   - Add type check flags
   - Add state signals in useEffect
   - Add type-specific config building logic
   - Add form fields in JSX

6. **Test with E2E**:
   - Use `mockChannelsStatus()` to mock backend
   - Test form field rendering, validation, submission
   - Test channel display in list

---

This is the complete pattern used throughout the codebase. All channel UIs follow this architecture: reactive signals for state, Preact/HTM for rendering, shared validation utilities, type-based branching for channel-specific fields, and CSS classes for styling.

```
     1→# Channels
     2→
     3→Moltis connects to messaging platforms through **channels**. Each channel type
     4→has a distinct inbound mode, determining how it receives messages, and a set of
     5→capabilities that control what features are available.
     6→
     7→## Supported Channels
     8→
     9→| Channel | Inbound Mode | Public URL Required | Key Capabilities |
    10→|---------|-------------|--------------------|--------------------|
    11→| Telegram | Polling | No | Streaming, voice ingest, reactions, OTP, location |
    12→| Discord | Gateway (WebSocket) | No | Streaming, interactive messages, threads, voice ingest, reactions |
    13→| Matrix | Gateway (sync loop) | No | Streaming, voice ingest, interactive polls, threads, reactions, OTP, location, encrypted chats, device verification, ownership bootstrap |
    14→| Microsoft Teams | Webhook | Yes | Streaming, interactive messages, threads, reactions |
    15→| WhatsApp | Gateway (WebSocket) | No | Streaming, voice ingest, OTP, pairing, location |
    16→| Slack | Socket Mode | No | Streaming, interactive messages, threads, reactions |
    17→
    18→## Inbound Modes
    19→
    20→### Polling
    21→
    22→The bot periodically fetches new messages from the platform API. No public URL
    23→or open port is needed. Used by Telegram.
    24→
    25→### Gateway / WebSocket
    26→
    27→The bot opens a persistent outbound WebSocket connection to the platform and
    28→receives events in real time, or uses a persistent sync loop over outbound HTTP.
    29→No public URL needed. Used by Discord, Matrix, and WhatsApp.
    30→
    31→### Socket Mode
    32→
    33→Similar to a gateway connection, but uses the platform's Socket Mode protocol.
    34→No public URL needed. Used by Slack.
    35→
    36→### Webhook
    37→
    38→The platform sends HTTP POST requests to a publicly reachable endpoint on your
    39→server. You must configure the messaging endpoint URL in the platform's
    40→settings. Used by Microsoft Teams.
    41→
    42→### None (Send-Only)
    43→
    44→For channels that only send outbound messages and do not receive inbound
    45→traffic. No channels currently use this mode, but it is available for future
    46→integrations (e.g. email, SMS).
    47→
    48→## Capabilities Reference
    49→
    50→| Capability | Description |
    51→|-----------|-------------|
    52→| `supports_outbound` | Can send messages to users |
    53→| `supports_streaming` | Can stream partial responses (typing/editing) |
    54→| `supports_interactive` | Can send interactive components (buttons, menus) |
    55→| `supports_threads` | Can reply in threads |
    56→| `supports_voice_ingest` | Can receive and transcribe voice messages |
    57→| `supports_pairing` | Requires device pairing (QR code) |
    58→| `supports_otp` | Supports OTP-based sender approval |
    59→| `supports_reactions` | Can add/remove emoji reactions |
    60→| `supports_location` | Can receive and process location data |
```

     1→# Telegram
     2→
     3→Moltis can connect to Telegram as a bot, letting you chat with your agent from
     4→any Telegram conversation. The integration uses Telegram's
     5→[Bot API](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api) with long polling — no public URL
     6→or webhook endpoint is required.
     7→
     8→## How It Works
     9→
    10→```
    11→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    12→│                 Telegram Bot API                      │
    13→│            (api.telegram.org/bot...)                  │
    14→└──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
    15→                   │  long polling (getUpdates)
    16→                   ▼
    17→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    18→│              moltis-telegram crate                    │
    19→│  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐  │
    20→│  │  Handler   │  │  Outbound  │  │     Plugin     │  │
    21→│  │ (inbound)  │  │ (replies)  │  │  (lifecycle)   │  │
    22→│  └────────────┘  └────────────┘  └────────────────┘  │
    23→└──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
    24→                   │
    25→                   ▼
    26→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    27→│                 Moltis Gateway                        │
    28→│         (chat dispatch, tools, memory)                │
    29→└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    30→```
    31→
    32→The bot connects **outward** to Telegram's servers via polling. No port
    33→forwarding, public domain, or TLS certificate is needed. This makes it easy to
    34→run on a home machine or behind a NAT.
    35→
    36→## Prerequisites
    37→
    38→Before configuring Moltis, create a Telegram bot:
    39→
    40→1. Open Telegram and message [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather)
    41→2. Send `/newbot` and follow the prompts to choose a name and username
    42→3. Copy the bot token (e.g. `123456:ABC-DEF1234ghIkl-zyx57W2v1u123ew11`)
    43→
    44→```admonish warning
    45→The bot token is a secret — treat it like a password. Never commit it to
    46→version control. Moltis stores it with `secrecy::Secret` and redacts it from
    47→logs, but your `moltis.toml` file is plain text on disk. Consider using
    48→[Vault](vault.md) for encryption at rest.
    49→```
    50→
    51→## Configuration
    52→
    53→Add a `[channels.telegram.<account-id>]` section to your `moltis.toml`:
    54→
    55→```toml
    56→[channels.telegram.my-bot]
    57→token = "123456:ABC-DEF1234ghIkl-zyx57W2v1u123ew11"
    58→```
    59→
    60→Make sure `"telegram"` is included in `channels.offered` so the Web UI shows
    61→the Telegram option:
    62→
    63→```toml
    64→[channels]
    65→offered = ["telegram"]
    66→```
    67→
    68→### Configuration Fields
    69→
    70→| Field | Required | Default | Description |
    71→|-------|----------|---------|-------------|
    72→| `token` | **yes** | — | Bot token from @BotFather |
    73→| `dm_policy` | no | `"allowlist"` | Who can DM the bot: `"open"`, `"allowlist"`, or `"disabled"` |
    74→| `group_policy` | no | `"open"` | Who can talk to the bot in groups: `"open"`, `"allowlist"`, or `"disabled"` |
    75→| `mention_mode` | no | `"mention"` | When the bot responds in groups: `"always"`, `"mention"` (only when @mentioned), or `"none"` |
    76→| `allowlist` | no | `[]` | User IDs or usernames allowed to DM the bot (when `dm_policy = "allowlist"`) |
    77→| `group_allowlist` | no | `[]` | Group/chat IDs allowed to interact with the bot |
    78→| `model` | no | — | Override the default model for this channel |
    79→| `model_provider` | no | — | Provider for the overridden model |
    80→| `reply_to_message` | no | `false` | Send bot responses as Telegram replies to the user's message |

  "file_path": "/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/helix-epoch/docs/src/nostr.md",
  "content": "# Nostr\n\nMoltis can receive and send encrypted direct messages over\n[Nostr](https://nostr.com), the decentralized social protocol. The integration\nuses [NIP-04](https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/04.md)\nencrypted DMs (kind:4) and connects to relays via `nostr-sdk` — no public URL\nor server infrastructure is required.\n\n## How It Works\n\n```\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│              Nostr Relay Network                      │\n│   (relay.damus.io, nos.lol, relay.nostr.band, ...)   │\n└──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘\n                   │  WebSocket subscription (kind:4)\n                   ▼\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                moltis-nostr crate                     │\n│  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐  │\n│  │    Bus     │  │  Outbound  │  │     Plugin     │  │\n│  │ (inbound)  │  │ (replies)  │  │  (lifecycle)   │  │\n│  └────────────┘  └────────────┘  └────────────────┘  │\n└──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘\n                   │\n                   ▼\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                 Moltis Gateway                        │\n│         (chat dispatch, tools, memory)                │\n└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\nThe bot connects **outward** to Nostr relays via WebSocket. No port forwarding,\npublic domain, or TLS certificate is needed. Messages are end-to-end encrypted\nbetween the sender and the bot using NIP-04.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\nBefore configuring Moltis, you need a Nostr secret key:\n\n1. Generate a new key pair using any Nostr client (e.g.\n   [Damus](https://damus.io), [Amethyst](https://github.com/vitorpamplona/amethyst),\n   or a key generation tool)\n2. Copy the secret key — either the `nsec1...` bech32 format or the 64-character\n   hex format\n3. Note the corresponding public key (`npub1...`) to share with users who want to\n   message the bot\n\n```admonish warning\nThe secret key is highly sensitive — it controls the bot's Nostr identity.\nNever commit it to version control. Moltis stores it with `secrecy::Secret` and\nredacts it from logs, but your `moltis.toml` file is plain text on disk.\nConsider using [Vault](vault.md) for encryption at rest.\n```\n\n## Configuration\n\nAdd a `[channels.nostr.<account-id>]` section to your `moltis.toml`:\n\n```toml\n[channels.nostr.my-bot]\nsecret_key = \"nsec1...\"\nrelays = [\"wss://relay.damus.io\", \"wss://relay.nostr.band\", \"wss://nos.lol\"]\ndm_policy = \"allowlist\"\nallowed_pubkeys = [\"npub1abc...\", \"npub1def...\"]\n```\n\nMake sure `\"nostr\"` is included in `channels.offered` (it is by default):\n\n```toml\n[channels]\noffered = [\"telegram\", \"discord\", \"slack\", \"matrix\", \"nostr\"]\n```\n\n### Configuration Fields\n\n| Field | Required | Default | Description |\n|-------|----------|---------|-------------|\n| `secret_key` | **yes** | — | Nostr secret key (`nsec1...` bech32 or 64-char hex) |\n| `relays` | no | `[\"wss://relay.damus.io\", \"wss://relay.nostr.band\", \"wss://nos.lol\"]` | Relay WebSocket URLs to connect to |\n| `dm_policy` | no | `\"allowlist\"` | Who can DM the bot: `\"open\"`, `\"allowlist\"`, or `\"disabled\"` |\n| `allowed_pubkeys` | no | `[]` | Public keys allowed to DM (`npub1...` or hex, when `dm_policy = \"allowlist\"`) |\n| `enabled` | no | `true` | Whether this account is active |\n| `model` | no | — | Override the default model for this channel |\n| `model_provider` | no | — | Provider for the overridden model |\n| `otp_self_approval` | no | `true` | Allow non-allowlisted senders to self-approve via OTP code |\n| `otp_cooldown_secs` | no | `300` | Cooldown after 3 failed OTP attempts |\n| `profile.name` | no | — | NIP-01 profile display name |\n| `profile.display_name` | no | — | NIP-01 longer display name |\n| `profile.about` | no | — | NIP-01 bio / about text |\n| `profile.picture` | no | — | NIP-01 avatar URL (HTTPS) |\n| `profile.nip05` | no | — | NIP-05 identifier (e.g. `bot@example.com`) |\n\n### Full Example\n\n```toml\n[channels.nostr.my-bot]\nsecret_key = \"nsec1qqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqspcgef\"\nrelays = [\n  \"wss://relay.damus.io\",\n  \"wss://relay.nostr.band\",\n  \"wss://nos.lol\",\n]\ndm_policy = \"allowlist\"\nallowed_pubkeys = [\n  \"npub1abc123...\",\n]\nmodel = \"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514\"\nmodel_provider = \"anthropic\"\notp_self_approval = true\notp_cooldown_secs = 300\n\n[channels.nostr.my-bot.profile]\nname = \"Moltis Bot\"\nabout = \"AI assistant on Nostr\"\nnip05 = \"bot@example.com\"\n```\n\n## Access Control\n\n### DM Policy\n\n- **`allowlist`** (default) — Only public keys in `allowed_pubkeys` can message\n  the bot. Unknown senders receive an OTP challenge if `otp_self_approval` is\n  enabled, or are silently ignored.\n- **`open`** — Anyone can DM the bot.\n- **`disabled`** — All inbound DMs are ignored.\n\n### OTP Self-Approval\n\nWhen `otp_self_approval` is enabled and a non-allowlisted sender messages the\nbot, the sender appears in the Senders tab of the web UI where they can be\napproved or denied. This works the same as OTP for Telegram and Matrix.\n\n## NIP-04 Encryption\n\nAll messages between the bot and users are encrypted using\n[NIP-04](https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/04.md) (kind:4\nevents). The bot can also decrypt inbound NIP-04 messages from any client that\nsupports this standard.\n\nNIP-44 and NIP-17 (gift-wrapped DMs) are planned for future releases.\n\n## Relay Health\n\nThe bot maintains persistent WebSocket connections to all configured relays.\nThe health probe reports the number of connected relays (e.g. \"2/3 relays\nconnected\"). If all relays disconnect, the bot will automatically attempt to\nreconnect via `nostr-sdk`'s built-in reconnection logic.\n"
}

     1→// Shared Playwright test fixture with automatic error-context capture.
     2→//
     3→// Every spec file should import { test, expect } from this module instead of
     4→// from "@playwright/test".  On failure the fixture attaches a markdown
     5→// snapshot of every open page (URL, title, visible text) so CI logs contain
     6→// enough context to diagnose failures without downloading trace artifacts.
     7→
     8→const { test: base, expect } = require("@playwright/test");
     9→
    10→var test = base.extend({
    11→	page: async ({ page, context }, use, testInfo) => {
    12→		await use(page);
    13→
    14→		if (testInfo.status !== testInfo.expectedStatus) {
    15→			var pages = context.pages();
    16→			var parts = [];
    17→
    18→			for (var i = 0; i < pages.length; i++) {
    19→				var p = pages[i];
    20→				try {
    21→					if (p.isClosed()) {
    22→						parts.push(`### Page ${i + 1}: (closed)`);
    23→						continue;
    24→					}
    25→					var url = p.url();
    26→					var title = await p.title().catch(() => "(unknown)");
    27→					var text = await p
    28→						.evaluate(() => document.body?.innerText?.slice(0, 3000) || "")
    29→						.catch(() => "(unavailable)");
    30→					parts.push(`### Page ${i + 1}: ${title}\n- **URL**: ${url}\n\n\`\`\`\n${text}\n\`\`\``);

Both follow-ups are now complete. Here's the summary of the second commit:

## Follow-up Implementation Complete

### Web UI (`page-channels.js`)
- **AddNostrModal** — form with secret key (password input), relays (comma-separated, pre-filled with defaults), DM policy select, allowed pubkeys allowlist, default model selector, advanced JSON config
- **Connect Nostr** button in the channel picker (gated by `channels.offered`)
- **EditChannelModal** — Nostr support with relay editing and secret key update
- **`channelLabel("nostr")`** returns "Nostr"

### E2E Tests (`channels-nostr.spec.js`)
- 4 test cases:
  1. Connect button visible when nostr is offered
  2. Add modal has correct fields with proper types/defaults
  3. Required field validation works (account ID, secret key)
  4. Nostr channel displays in channel list with mock status data

### Documentation (`docs/src/nostr.md`)
- Architecture diagram
- Prerequisites (key generation)
- Full config field reference table
- Complete TOML example
- Access control (DM policy, OTP)
- NIP-04 encryption description
- Relay health monitoring

### Total across both commits
- **25 new/modified files, ~2,200 LOC added**
- **23 Rust unit tests + 4 E2E Playwright tests**
- Crate compiles cleanly, clippy passes, format passes, all existing tests unbroken

> AGENT

Actually, looking at this more carefully: `matrix` was already going through `extra` before, and the `all_channel_configs()` method iterates both named and extra. Since the gateway iterates `all_channel_configs()` and tries to find a registered plugin for each, matrix configs were working fine through `extra`. By adding it as a named field now, existing TOML configs with `[channels.matrix.my-bot]` will now deserialize into `self.matrix` instead of `self.extra["matrix"]`. This is actually a safe change — serde prioritizes named fields over flatten. And both paths feed into `all_channel_configs()`.

But this is an unnecessary side-effect of the Nostr work. Let me revert the `matrix` promotion and only keep `nostr`:

The contract tests expect `start_account` to work with an empty `{}` config. For Nostr, the plugin requires at minimum a valid secret key. But the Nostr plugin's `start_account` with `enabled: false` returns early successfully. With empty config the `secret_key` defaults to empty and `enabled` defaults to `true`, so it would try to parse an empty key and fail. The contract tests use `TestPlugin` from the registry, not real plugins, so they wouldn't apply directly. The contract is designed for the `TestPlugin` — real channel plugins "only need per-channel descriptor-coherence tests" per the docstring.

## Integration Test Summary

I've mapped out the integration test infrastructure in this codebase. Here are the key findings:

### 1. **API Key Environment Variables**
Each provider test uses a standard naming convention: `{PROVIDER_NAME}_API_KEY`

Examples:
- `OPENAI_API_KEY`
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
- `GEMINI_API_KEY`
- `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`
- `FIREWORKS_API_KEY`
- `MISTRAL_API_KEY`
- `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`
- `KIMI_API_KEY` (for kimi-code provider)
- `MOONSHOT_API_KEY`
- `MINIMAX_API_KEY`
- `Z_API_KEY` (for zai provider)

### 2. **Test Gating Pattern**
All provider integration tests use `#[ignore]` attribute to gate them by default:
```rust
#[tokio::test]
#[ignore]
async fn system_prompt_is_received() { ... }
```

Run individually with: `cargo test --test openai_integration -- --ignored`

Helper functions check for the env var and panic if missing:
```rust
fn api_key() -> Secret<String> {
    let key = std::env::var("OPENAI_API_KEY")
        .expect("OPENAI_API_KEY must be set for integration tests");
    Secret::new(key)
}
```

### 3. **File Locations**
All provider integration tests are in: `/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/helix-epoch/crates/providers/tests/`

Files follow pattern: `{provider}_integration.rs`
- `/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/helix-epoch/crates/providers/tests/openai_integration.rs`
- `/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/helix-epoch/crates/providers/tests/anthropic_integration.rs`
- `/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/helix-epoch/crates/providers/tests/gemini_integration.rs`
- `/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/helix-epoch/crates/providers/tests/deepseek_integration.rs`
- etc. (11 total provider integration tests)

### 4. **CI Integration**
GitHub Actions workflow: `/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/helix-epoch/.github/workflows/provider-integration.yml`

- Runs daily at 06:00 UTC (scheduled cron job)
- Uses GitHub Secrets to pass API keys from `secrets.{PROVIDER}_API_KEY` → env var
- Gracefully skips tests if secret is not configured (sets `SKIP=true`)
- Runs tests sequentially (`max-parallel: 1`) to avoid rate limits
- Uses `continue-on-error: true` to prevent single provider downtime from failing CI
- Command: `cargo test --test {test_name} -- --ignored --test-threads=1`

**CI Secret Mapping Pattern:**
```yaml
env:
  PROVIDER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
run: |
  if [ -z "$PROVIDER_API_KEY" ]; then
    echo "::warning::Secret not configured — skipping tests"
    echo "SKIP=true" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "OPENAI_API_KEY=$PROVIDER_API_KEY" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
```

### 5. **No Channel-Specific Integration Tests**
No integration tests found in `crates/telegram/tests/`, `crates/matrix/tests/`, or `crates/nostr/tests/` directories. Channel implementations appear to rely on unit tests and gateway integration tests only.

### 6. **Test Structure**
Each integration test covers:
- System prompt handling (streaming + non-streaming)
- Tool call round-trips (streaming + non-streaming)
- Multi-turn tool use
- API probing (connection validation)
- Stream event emission (Delta, Done)
- Model catalog health checks
- New model detection via API

### 7. **Key Files**

pub fn encrypt<T>(
    secret_key: &SecretKey,
    public_key: &PublicKey,
    content: T,
    version: Version,
) -> Result<String, Error>
where
    T: AsRef<[u8]>,
{
    encrypt_with_rng(&mut OsRng, secret_key, public_key, content, version)
}

/// Encrypt
---
pub fn decrypt<T>(
    secret_key: &SecretKey,
    public_key: &PublicKey,
    payload: T,
) -> Result<String, Error>
where
    T: AsRef<[u8]>,
{
    let bytes: Vec<u8> = decrypt_to_bytes(secret_key, public_key, payload)?;
    String::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|_| Error::Utf8Encode)
}

    51→impl ChannelOutbound for NostrOutbound {
    52→    async fn send_text(
    53→        &self,
    54→        account_id: &str,
    55→        to: &str,
    56→        text: &str,
    57→        _reply_to: Option<&str>,
    58→    ) -> ChannelResult<()> {
    59→        let (client, keys, recipient) = self.resolve(account_id, to).await?;
    60→
    61→        // Encrypt with NIP-04
    62→        let encrypted = nip04::encrypt(keys.secret_key(), &recipient, text).map_err(|e| {
    63→            moltis_channels::Error::external(
    64→                "nostr",
    65→                crate::error::Error::Encryption(format!("NIP-04 encrypt failed: {e}")),
    66→            )
    67→        })?;
    68→
    69→        // Build and publish kind:4 event
    70→        let tag = Tag::public_key(recipient);
    71→        let builder = EventBuilder::new(Kind::EncryptedDirectMessage, &encrypted).tag(tag);
    72→
    73→        client
    74→            .send_event_builder(builder)
    75→            .await
    76→            .map_err(|e| moltis_channels::Error::external("nostr", crate::error::Error::Sdk(e)))?;
    77→
    78→        let npub = recipient.to_bech32().unwrap_or_else(|_| recipient.to_hex());

    80→
    81→        Ok(())
    82→    }

> AGENT

`moltis-matrix` is also optional but appears in `metrics`. That works because Cargo treats `optional-dep/feature` as implying the dep — it enables both `dep:moltis-matrix` AND `moltis-matrix/metrics`. But that means enabling `metrics` would also pull in `moltis-matrix`! Let me check if this is actually the intended behavior by looking at what `default` includes:

Looking at the gateway defaults: `matrix` and `metrics` are both in `default`. So in practice both are always on. Same for `nostr` — it's in `default`. So adding `moltis-nostr/metrics` to the `metrics` feature is fine, since both `nostr` and `metrics` are in `default`.

But to be safe with non-default builds, I should use the `dep?/feature` syntax:

> TOOL

  "new_string": "  \"moltis-nostr?/metrics\",\n]"

> AGENT

Everything is done. Here's what you need to do for real integration tests:

**Create two Nostr key pairs:**

```bash
# Generate with any tool — e.g. nak (https://github.com/fiatjaf/nak)
nak key generate   # → bot nsec + npub
nak key generate   # → sender nsec + npub
```

**Set as environment variables:**
```bash
export NOSTR_TEST_SECRET_KEY="nsec1..."   # Bot identity
export NOSTR_TEST_SENDER_KEY="nsec1..."   # Simulated sender
```

**Run integration tests:**
```bash
cargo test -p moltis-nostr --test nostr_integration -- --ignored
```

**For CI**, add `NOSTR_TEST_SECRET_KEY` and `NOSTR_TEST_SENDER_KEY` to your GitHub secrets, following the same pattern as the provider integration tests in `.github/workflows/provider-integration.yml`.

**Summary of this commit (5th in the series):**

| Feature | What was added |
|---|---|
| **Metrics** | 9 metric constants (counters, gauges, histogram), instrumentation in bus.rs, outbound.rs, plugin.rs |
| **NIP-44** | Fallback decryption in inbound pipeline, `nip44` feature enabled on `nostr-sdk` |
| **Integration tests** | 5 `#[ignore]` tests: key parsing, relay connect, profile publish, DM round-trip, NIP-44 crypto |

> AGENT

The issue is likely that `nostr-sdk`'s `Event` notification deduplicates — it says "sent only the first time the Event is seen" and "Events sent by this client are not included". But the DM is sent by the *sender* client, not the bot client, so that shouldn't be it. The issue is more likely that the `Event` notification only fires for new events matching the subscription, but the subscription filter uses `.pubkey(bot_pubkey)` which filters by the `p` tag. Let me check if the filter is correct:

The NIP-04 DM kind:4 uses a `p` tag pointing to the recipient. So `Filter::pubkey(bot_pubkey)` should match DMs TO the bot. But `nostr-sdk`'s `pubkey` filter might match the event's `pubkey` field (the author), not the `p` tag. Let me check:

> AGENT

Good — `pubkey()` filters on `#p` tag (the recipient in a DM), which is correct. The issue must be relay propagation timing. Let me check if we're using `RelayPoolNotification::Event` which deduplicates, vs `Message` which gives raw messages:

Looking at the notification docs: "sent only the first time the Event is seen." — this means if the bot client somehow already received the event via EOSE (end of stored events), it won't fire again. The `since` filter should prevent that, but timing can be tricky.

Let me switch to using `Message` notifications which fire for every relay message:

File: crates/nostr/src/plugin.rs:165
Body: <a href="#"><img alt="P1" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p1.svg?v=7" align="top"></a> **Subscription loop uses a disconnected config clone**

`loop_config` is a brand-new `Arc::new(RwLock::new(nostr_config.clone()))`, completely independent from `state.config`. When `update_account_config` is called (e.g. the user changes DM policy or the allowlist via the UI), it writes to `state.config` — but the running subscription loop reads from `loop_config` and never sees the update. Access-control changes silently take no effect until the account is stopped and restarted.

Fix: store the shared `Arc<RwLock<NostrAccountConfig>>` in `AccountState` instead of a plain value, then pass the same `Arc` to the loop *and* store it on the state so `update_account_config` can write through it.

---
File: crates/nostr/src/plugin.rs:233
Body: <a href="#"><img alt="P1" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p1.svg?v=7" align="top"></a> <a href="#"><img alt="security" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/Security.svg?v=1" align="top"></a> **Editing a channel via UI permanently corrupts the stored private key**

`account_config_json` returns `"[REDACTED]"` for the `nsec` field (via `RedactedConfig`). In the edit modal, `addChannelCredentials` falls back to `cfg.secret_key` when the credential input is blank, so the literal `"[REDACTED]"` string gets sent as the new key value. `update_account_config` deserialises this without checking it and stores it in `state.config`. On the next account restart, `keys::derive_keys` fails because the sentinel is not a valid private key.

The Matrix plugin prevents this by checking whether the incoming credential value equals the redacted sentinel before overwriting the existing credential, and substituting the current stored value if it matches. Nostr needs the same merge guard in `update_account_config`.

---
File: crates/nostr/src/bus.rs:186
Body: <a href="#"><img alt="P2" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p2.svg?v=7" align="top"></a> **tokio `RwLockReadGuard` held across an `.await` point**

`cfg` (acquired at line 140) is still live when `event_sink.emit(...).await` is called at line 166. Holding a `tokio::sync::RwLockReadGuard` across an async yield point blocks any task waiting for a write lock for the entire duration of the emit. Once the config-isolation bug above is fixed and the loop starts sharing the config `Arc` with `update_account_config`, this becomes a latent write-stall or, on a single-threaded runtime, a deadlock.

Drop the guard before the emit by extracting only what you need into local variables first.

---
File: crates/nostr/src/bus.rs:94
Body: <a href="#"><img alt="P2" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p2.svg?v=7" align="top"></a> **No reconnection on relay pool shutdown**

When `RelayPoolNotification::Shutdown` fires the loop exits permanently; the only recovery is an external account restart. If a relay pool disconnects transiently (network blip, relay restart) the bot goes dark until an operator intervenes. Consider a reconnect-with-backoff loop, or at minimum propagate the shutdown so the plugin layer can restart the account automatically.

---
File: crates/nostr/src/access.rs:29
Body: <a href="#"><img alt="P2" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p2.svg?v=7" align="top"></a> **Allowlist re-parsed on every inbound DM**

`normalize_pubkeys` calls `PublicKey::parse` for every entry on every message arrival when the policy is `Allowlist`. These strings are unchanged between messages, so the work is fully redundant. Pre-parse the allowlist at config-load time and store the resulting `Vec<PublicKey>` in `NostrAccountConfig` (or cache it in `AccountState`). Compare the sender against that pre-parsed slice here instead of re-parsing each time.
```

   261→                let connected_count = relays
   262→                    .values()
   263→                    .filter(|r| r.status() == RelayStatus::Connected)
   264→                    .count();
   265→                let total = relays.len();
   266→
   267→                let npub = state
   268→                    .keys
   269→                    .public_key()
   270→                    .to_bech32()
   271→                    .unwrap_or_else(|_| state.keys.public_key().to_hex());
   272→                Ok(ChannelHealthSnapshot {
   273→                    connected: connected_count > 0,
   274→                    account_id: account_id.to_string(),
   275→                    details: Some(format!("{connected_count}/{total} relays connected")),
   276→                    extra: Some(serde_json::json!({
   277→                        "pubkey": npub,
   278→                        "connected_relays": connected_count,
   279→                        "total_relays": total,
   280→                    })),
   281→                })
   282→            },
   283→            None => Ok(ChannelHealthSnapshot {
   284→                connected: false,
   285→                account_id: account_id.to_string(),
   286→                details: Some("account not found".to_string()),
   287→                extra: None,
   288→            }),
   289→        }
   290→    }
   291→}
   292→
   293→impl ChannelOtpProvider for NostrPlugin {
   294→    fn pending_otp_challenges(&self, account_id: &str) -> Vec<OtpChallengeInfo> {
   295→        self.otp_challenges(account_id)
   296→    }
   297→}

     1→//! Nostr relay subscription loop — inbound DM pipeline.
     2→//!
     3→//! Subscribes to kind:4 (NIP-04 encrypted DMs) addressed to the bot's pubkey.
     4→//! Events flow through dedup, self-message filtering, access control, and
     5→//! decryption before being dispatched to the gateway via `ChannelEventSink`.
     6→
     7→use std::sync::Arc;
     8→
     9→use {
    10→    nostr_sdk::prelude::{
    11→        Client, Event, Filter, Keys, Kind, PublicKey, RelayPoolNotification, Timestamp, ToBech32,
    12→        nip04, nip44,
    13→    },
    14→    tokio::sync::RwLock,
    15→    tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken,
    16→};
    17→
    18→use crate::{
    19→    access::{self, AccessDenied},
    20→    config::NostrAccountConfig,
    21→    seen::SeenTracker,
    22→};
    23→
    24→#[cfg(feature = "metrics")]
    25→use moltis_metrics::{counter, nostr as nostr_metrics};
    26→
    27→/// Maximum plaintext message size in bytes.
    28→const MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024;
    29→
    30→/// Run the relay subscription loop for a single Nostr account.
    31→///
    32→/// Subscribes to NIP-04 DMs (kind:4) targeted at `bot_pubkey` and dispatches
    33→/// inbound messages to the gateway. Runs until `cancel` is triggered.
    34→pub async fn run_subscription_loop(
    35→    client: Client,
    36→    keys: Keys,
    37→    config: Arc<RwLock<NostrAccountConfig>>,
    38→    account_id: String,
    39→    event_sink: Arc<dyn moltis_channels::ChannelEventSink>,
    40→    cancel: CancellationToken,
    41→) {
    42→    let bot_pubkey = keys.public_key();
    43→    let now_secs =
    44→        u64::try_from(::time::OffsetDateTime::now_utc().unix_timestamp()).unwrap_or_default();
    45→    let since = Timestamp::from(now_secs);
    46→
    47→    let filter = Filter::new()
    48→        .kind(Kind::EncryptedDirectMessage)
    49→        .pubkey(bot_pubkey)
    50→        .since(since);
    51→
    52→    let npub = bot_pubkey
    53→        .to_bech32()
    54→        .unwrap_or_else(|_| bot_pubkey.to_hex());
    55→    tracing::info!(
    56→        account_id,
    57→        pubkey = %npub,
    58→        "starting Nostr DM subscription"
    59→    );
    60→
    61→    let mut seen = SeenTracker::new();
    62→
    63→    // Subscribe (single filter)
    64→    if let Err(e) = client.subscribe(filter, None).await {
    65→        tracing::error!(account_id, "failed to subscribe: {e}");
    66→        return;
    67→    }
    68→
    69→    let mut notifications = client.notifications();
    70→
    71→    loop {
    72→        tokio::select! {
    73→            () = cancel.cancelled() => {
    74→                tracing::info!(account_id, "Nostr subscription cancelled");
    75→                break;
    76→            }
    77→            notification = notifications.recv() => {
    78→                match notification {
    79→                    Ok(RelayPoolNotification::Event { event, .. }) => {
    80→                        handle_event(
    81→                            &event,
    82→                            &keys,
    83→                            &bot_pubkey,
    84→                            since,
    85→                            &mut seen,
    86→                            &config,
    87→                            &account_id,
    88→                            &event_sink,
    89→                        ).await;
    90→                    }
    91→                    Ok(RelayPoolNotification::Shutdown) => {
    92→                        tracing::warn!(account_id, "relay pool shutdown");
    93→                        break;
    94→                    }
    95→                    Ok(_) => {} // Message, etc.
    96→                    Err(e) => {
    97→                        tracing::warn!(account_id, "notification channel error: {e}");
    98→                    }
    99→                }
   100→            }
   101→        }
   102→    }
   103→
   104→    tracing::info!(account_id, "Nostr subscription loop exited");
   105→}
   106→
   107→/// Process a single inbound event through the pipeline.
   108→#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
   109→async fn handle_event(
   110→    event: &Event,
   111→    keys: &Keys,
   112→    bot_pubkey: &PublicKey,
   113→    since: Timestamp,
   114→    seen: &mut SeenTracker,
   115→    config: &Arc<RwLock<NostrAccountConfig>>,
   116→    account_id: &str,
   117→    event_sink: &Arc<dyn moltis_channels::ChannelEventSink>,
   118→) {
   119→    // 1. Skip non-DM events
   120→    if event.kind != Kind::EncryptedDirectMessage {
   121→        return;
   122→    }
   123→
   124→    // 2. Dedup check
   125→    if seen.check_and_insert(&event.id) {
   126→        return;
   127→    }
   128→
   129→    // 3. Skip self-messages
   130→    if event.pubkey == *bot_pubkey {
   131→        return;
   132→    }
   133→
   134→    // 4. Skip stale events
   135→    if event.created_at < since {
   136→        return;
   137→    }
   138→
   139→    // 5. Access control (BEFORE decryption)
   140→    let cfg = config.read().await;
   141→    let access_result =
   142→        access::check_dm_access(&event.pubkey, &cfg.dm_policy, &cfg.allowed_pubkeys);
   143→
   144→    let sender_hex = event.pubkey.to_hex();
   145→    let sender_npub = event
   146→        .pubkey
   147→        .to_bech32()
   148→        .unwrap_or_else(|_| sender_hex.clone());
   149→
   150→    match &access_result {
   151→        Ok(()) => {},
   152→        Err(AccessDenied::Disabled) => {
   153→            #[cfg(feature = "metrics")]
   154→            counter!(nostr_metrics::ACCESS_CONTROL_DENIALS_TOTAL, "reason" => "disabled")
   155→                .increment(1);
   156→            tracing::debug!(account_id, sender = sender_hex, "DM rejected: disabled");
   157→            return;
   158→        },
   159→        Err(AccessDenied::NotAllowlisted) => {
   160→            #[cfg(feature = "metrics")]
   161→            counter!(nostr_metrics::ACCESS_CONTROL_DENIALS_TOTAL, "reason" => "not_allowlisted")
   162→                .increment(1);
   163→            if cfg.otp_self_approval {
   164→                #[cfg(feature = "metrics")]
   165→                counter!(nostr_metrics::OTP_CHALLENGES_TOTAL).increment(1);
   166→                event_sink
   167→                    .emit(moltis_channels::ChannelEvent::InboundMessage {
   168→                        channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,
   169→                        account_id: account_id.to_string(),
   170→                        peer_id: sender_hex.clone(),
   171→                        username: Some(sender_npub.clone()),
   172→                        sender_name: None,
   173→                        message_count: None,
   174→                        access_granted: false,
   175→                    })
   176→                    .await;
   177→                return;
   178→            }
   179→            tracing::debug!(
   180→                account_id,
   181→                sender = sender_hex,
   182→                "DM rejected: not allowlisted"
   183→            );
   184→            return;
   185→        },
   186→    }
   187→    drop(cfg);
   188→
   189→    // 6. Decrypt content — try NIP-04 first, fall back to NIP-44
   190→    let plaintext = match nip04::decrypt(keys.secret_key(), &event.pubkey, &event.content) {
   191→        Ok(text) => text,
   192→        Err(_nip04_err) => {
   193→            // NIP-04 failed — try NIP-44 (some clients use it for kind:4 events)
   194→            match nip44::decrypt(keys.secret_key(), &event.pubkey, &event.content) {
   195→                Ok(text) => text,
   196→                Err(nip44_err) => {
   197→                    #[cfg(feature = "metrics")]
   198→                    counter!(nostr_metrics::DECRYPT_ERRORS_TOTAL).increment(1);
   199→                    tracing::warn!(
   200→                        account_id,
   201→                        event_id = %event.id,
   202→                        "decrypt failed (NIP-04 and NIP-44): {nip44_err}"
   203→                    );
   204→                    return;
   205→                },
   206→            }
   207→        },
   208→    };
   209→
   210→    // 7. Size validation
   211→    let text = if plaintext.len() > MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES {
   212→        tracing::warn!(account_id, len = plaintext.len(), "DM exceeds size limit");
   213→        &plaintext[..MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES]
   214→    } else {
   215→        &plaintext
   216→    };
   217→
   218→    // 8. Emit inbound event
   219→    #[cfg(feature = "metrics")]
   220→    counter!(nostr_metrics::MESSAGES_RECEIVED_TOTAL).increment(1);
   221→
   222→    event_sink
   223→        .emit(moltis_channels::ChannelEvent::InboundMessage {
   224→            channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,
   225→            account_id: account_id.to_string(),
   226→            peer_id: sender_hex.clone(),
   227→            username: Some(sender_npub.clone()),
   228→            sender_name: None,
   229→            message_count: None,
   230→            access_granted: true,
   231→        })
   232→        .await;
   233→
   234→    // 9. Dispatch to gateway
   235→    let reply_to = moltis_channels::ChannelReplyTarget {
   236→        channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,
   237→        account_id: account_id.to_string(),
   238→        chat_id: sender_hex,
   239→        message_id: Some(event.id.to_hex()),
   240→        thread_id: None,
   241→    };
   242→
   243→    let meta = moltis_channels::ChannelMessageMeta {
   244→        channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,
   245→        sender_name: None,
   246→        username: Some(sender_npub),
   247→        message_kind: Some(moltis_channels::ChannelMessageKind::Text),
   248→        model: None,
   249→        audio_filename: None,
   250→    };
   251→
   252→    event_sink.dispatch_to_chat(text, reply_to, meta).await;
   253→}
   254→
   255→#[cfg(test)]
   256→mod tests {
   257→    use super::*;
   258→
   259→    #[test]
   260→    fn max_message_size_is_reasonable() {
   261→        assert_eq!(MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES, 64 * 1024);
   262→    }
   263→}
   264→

     1→//! DM access control for Nostr channels.
     2→//!
     3→//! Reuses `DmPolicy` from `moltis_channels::gating` and maps Nostr pubkeys
     4→//! to the allowlist/OTP gating model used by other channels.

     6→use {moltis_channels::gating::DmPolicy, nostr_sdk::prelude::PublicKey};

     8→use crate::keys::normalize_pubkeys;
     9→
    10→/// Check whether a sender pubkey is authorized under the given DM policy.
    11→///
    12→/// Returns `Ok(())` if allowed, `Err(AccessDenied)` with a reason if not.
    13→pub fn check_dm_access(
    14→    sender: &PublicKey,
    15→    policy: &DmPolicy,
    16→    raw_allowlist: &[String],
    17→) -> Result<(), AccessDenied> {
    18→    match policy {
    19→        DmPolicy::Disabled => Err(AccessDenied::Disabled),
    20→        DmPolicy::Open => Ok(()),
    21→        DmPolicy::Allowlist => {
    22→            let allowed = normalize_pubkeys(raw_allowlist);
    23→            if allowed.iter().any(|pk| pk == sender) {
    24→                Ok(())
    25→            } else {
    26→                Err(AccessDenied::NotAllowlisted)
    27→            }
    28→        },
    29→    }
    30→}
    31→
    32→/// Reason a DM was denied.
    33→#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
    34→pub enum AccessDenied {
    35→    /// DMs are globally disabled for this account.
    36→    Disabled,
    37→    /// Sender pubkey is not in the allowlist.
    38→    NotAllowlisted,
    39→}
    40→
    41→impl std::fmt::Display for AccessDenied {
    42→    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
    43→        match self {
    44→            Self::Disabled => write!(f, "DMs are disabled"),
    45→            Self::NotAllowlisted => write!(f, "sender not in allowlist"),
    46→        }
    47→    }
    48→}

accounts\n            .get(account_id)\n            .map(|state| state.otp.list_pending())\n            .unwrap_or_default()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for NostrPlugin {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl ChannelPlugin for NostrPlugin {\n    fn id(&self) -> &str {\n        \"nostr\"\n    }\n\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"Nostr\"\n    }\n\n    async fn start_account(&mut self, account_id: &str, config: Value) -> ChannelResult<()> {\n        let nostr_config: NostrAccountConfig = serde_json::from_value(config).map_err(|e| {\n            moltis_channels::Error::invalid_input(format!(\"invalid nostr config: {e}\"))\n        })?;\n\n        if !nostr_config.enabled {\n            tracing::info!(account_id, \"nostr account disabled, skipping\");\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        // Parse keys\n        let bot_keys = keys::derive_keys(&nostr_config.secret_key).map_err(|e| {\n .unwrap_or_else(|_| bot_keys.public_key().to_hex());\n        tracing::info!(\n            account_id,\n            pubkey = %npub,\n            relays = ?nostr_config.relays,\n            \"starting Nostr account\"\n        );\n\n        // Build nostr-sdk client\n        let client = Client::new(bot_keys.clone());\n\n        // Add relays\n        for relay_url in &nostr_config.relays {\n relays\n        client.connect().await;\n\n        // Publish profile if configured\n        if let Some(ref prof) = nostr_config.profile\n            && let Err(e) = profile::publish_profile(&client, prof).await\n        {\n            tracing::warn!(account_id, \"failed to publish profile: {e}\");\n        }\n\n        let cancel = CancellationToken::new();\n\n        // Spawn subscription loop\n        let event_sink = self\n            .event_sink\n            .clone()\n            .ok_or_else(|| moltis_channels::Error::unavailable(\"event sink not configured\"))?;\n\n        // Pre-parse AccountState {\n            client,\n            keys: bot_keys,\n            config: shared_config,\n            cached_allowlist,\n            cancel,\n            otp: #[cfg(feature = \"metrics\")]\n        gauge!(nostr_metrics::ACTIVE_ACCOUNTS).set(self.accounts.read().await.len() as f64);\n\n        tracing::info!(account_id, \"Nostr account started\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn stop_account(&mut self, account_id: &str) -> ChannelResult<()> {\n        let state = self.accounts.write().await.remove(account_id);\n        if let Some(state) = state {\n            state.cancel.cancel();\n            state.client.disconnect().await;\n            #[cfg(feature = \"metrics\")]\n            gauge!(nostr_metrics::ACTIVE_ACCOUNTS).set(self.accounts.read().await.len() as f64);\n            tracing::info!(account_id, \"Nostr account stopped\");\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn self.accounts.blocking_read().keys().cloned().collect()\n    }\n\n    fn account_config(&self, account_id: &str) -> Option<Box<dyn ChannelConfigView>> {\n        let accounts = })\n    }\n\n    fn account_config_json(&self, account_id: &str) -> Option<Value> {\n        let accounts = self.accounts.blocking_read();\n        accounts.get(account_id).and_then(|s| {\n moltis_channels::Error::invalid_input(format!(\"invalid nostr config: {e}\"))\n            })?;\n\n        let accounts = self.accounts.blocking_read();\n        if let Some(state) = > AGENT

Pushed and all 5 review comments replied to. Summary of fixes:

| Review Comment | Fix |
|---|---|
| **P1 — Disconnected config clone** | `AccountState.config` is now `Arc<RwLock<NostrAccountConfig>>` shared between state and bus loop |
| **P1/security — Redacted key corruption** | `update_account_config` detects `[REDACTED]` sentinel and preserves existing key |
| **P2 — RwLockReadGuard across await** | Extract `dm_policy` + `otp_self_approval` into locals, drop guard before any `.await` |
| **P2 — No reconnection on shutdown** | Call `request_disable_account()` on pool shutdown so gateway can surface it |
| **P2 — Allowlist re-parsed every DM** | Pre-parsed `Vec<PublicKey>` cached in `AccountState`, refreshed on config update |

---
ID: 3069384546
File: crates/nostr/src/plugin.rs:165
Body: <a href="#"><img alt="P1" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p1.svg?v=7" align="top"></a> **Subscription loop uses a disconnected config clone**

`loop_config` is a brand-new `Arc::new(RwLock::new(nostr_config.clone()))`, completely independent from `state.config`. When `update_account_config` is called (e.g. the user changes DM policy or the allowlist via the UI), it writes to `state.config` — but the running subscription loop reads from `loop_config` and never sees the update. Access-control changes silently take no effect until the account is stopped and restarted.

Fix: store the shared `Arc<RwLock<NostrAccountConfig>>` in `AccountState` instead of a plain value, then pass the same `Arc` to the loop *and* store it on the state so `update_account_config` can write through it.

---
ID: 3069384564
File: crates/nostr/src/plugin.rs:233
Body: <a href="#"><img alt="P1" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p1.svg?v=7" align="top"></a> <a href="#"><img alt="security" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/Security.svg?v=1" align="top"></a> **Editing a channel via UI permanently corrupts the stored private key**

`account_config_json` returns `"[REDACTED]"` for the `nsec` field (via `RedactedConfig`). In the edit modal, `addChannelCredentials` falls back to `cfg.secret_key` when the credential input is blank, so the literal `"[REDACTED]"` string gets sent as the new key value. `update_account_config` deserialises this without checking it and stores it in `state.config`. On the next account restart, `keys::derive_keys` fails because the sentinel is not a valid private key.

The Matrix plugin prevents this by checking whether the incoming credential value equals the redacted sentinel before overwriting the existing credential, and substituting the current stored value if it matches. Nostr needs the same merge guard in `update_account_config`.

---
ID: 3069384607
File: crates/nostr/src/bus.rs:186
Body: <a href="#"><img alt="P2" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p2.svg?v=7" align="top"></a> **tokio `RwLockReadGuard` held across an `.await` point**

`cfg` (acquired at line 140) is still live when `event_sink.emit(...).await` is called at line 166. Holding a `tokio::sync::RwLockReadGuard` across an async yield point blocks any task waiting for a write lock for the entire duration of the emit. Once the config-isolation bug above is fixed and the loop starts sharing the config `Arc` with `update_account_config`, this becomes a latent write-stall or, on a single-threaded runtime, a deadlock.

Drop the guard before the emit by extracting only what you need into local variables first.

---
ID: 3069384629
File: crates/nostr/src/bus.rs:94
Body: <a href="#"><img alt="P2" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p2.svg?v=7" align="top"></a> **No reconnection on relay pool shutdown**

When `RelayPoolNotification::Shutdown` fires the loop exits permanently; the only recovery is an external account restart. If a relay pool disconnects transiently (network blip, relay restart) the bot goes dark until an operator intervenes. Consider a reconnect-with-backoff loop, or at minimum propagate the shutdown so the plugin layer can restart the account automatically.

---
ID: 3069384645
File: crates/nostr/src/access.rs:29
Body: <a href="#"><img alt="P2" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p2.svg?v=7" align="top"></a> **Allowlist re-parsed on every inbound DM**

`normalize_pubkeys` calls `PublicKey::parse` for every entry on every message arrival when the policy is `Allowlist`. These strings are unchanged between messages, so the work is fully redundant. Pre-parse the allowlist at config-load time and store the resulting `Vec<PublicKey>` in `NostrAccountConfig` (or cache it in `AccountState`). Compare the sender against that pre-parsed slice here instead of re-parsing each time.

---
ID: 3069401887
File: crates/nostr/src/bus.rs:232
Body: <a href="#"><img alt="P1" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p1.svg?v=7" align="top"></a> **UTF-8 boundary slice panics on long non-ASCII messages**

`&plaintext[..MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES]` panics with `'byte index 65536 is not a char boundary'` if the byte at position 65536 falls in the middle of a multi-byte codepoint (emoji, CJK, Arabic, etc.). If triggered, the panic propagates out of `handle_event` and terminates the spawned subscription loop task, silently killing that account's message processing.

```suggestion
    // 7. Size validation — truncate at a safe UTF-8 boundary
    let truncated;
    let text = if plaintext.len() > MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES {
        tracing::warn!(account_id, len = plaintext.len(), "DM exceeds size limit");
        let mut end = MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES;
        while !plaintext.is_char_boundary(end) {
            end -= 1;
        }
        truncated = &plaintext[..end];
        truncated
    } else {
        &plaintext
    };
```
```

The most widely used Nostr logo comes from the **mbarulli/nostr-logo** repository on GitHub, licensed CC0 (public domain). The purple color is `#662482`.

1. **Purple icon on white background**: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mbarulli/nostr-logo/main/SVG/nostr-icon-purple-on-white.svg`

3. **Purple icon, transparent background**: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mbarulli/nostr-logo/main/SVG/nostr-icon-purple-transparent.svg`

### Key details:
- **Brand color**: `#662482` (deep purple/violet)
- **Design**: Stylized lowercase "n" with a dot (eye-like element), inside a rounded rectangle (squircle) background
- **Designer**: Andrea Nicolini (aka Bembureda)
- **License**: CC0 1.0 Universal (public domain, no restrictions)
- **Viewbox**: 256x256
- **Note**: Nostr has no single "official" logo since it is a decentralized protocol, but this is the most widely recognized and used one across the ecosystem

Body: <a href="#"><img alt="P1" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p1.svg?v=7" align="top"></a> **Nostr OTP settings silently reset on every UI save**

`buildUpdateConfig` for Nostr doesn't include `otp_self_approval` or `otp_cooldown_secs`. `NostrAccountConfig` is annotated `#[serde(default)]`, so whenever the edit modal saves, both fields are reset to their defaults (`otp_self_approval: true`, `otp_cooldown_secs: 300`). A user who set `otp_self_approval: false` via the Advanced Config JSON patch will find DM access control silently re-enabled after the next ordinary edit.

The Matrix branch sets both fields explicitly; adding the same for Nostr (and corresponding `useSignal` state in the component) would prevent the reset. At minimum, read the existing values from `cfg` and echo them back if no dedicated UI fields are added yet:

```suggestion
		if (isNostr) {
			updateConfig.allowed_pubkeys = allowlistItems.value;
			// Preserve OTP settings that have no dedicated UI fields yet.
			updateConfig.otp_self_approval = cfg.otp_self_approval !== false;
			updateConfig.otp_cooldown_secs = cfg.otp_cooldown_secs ?? 300;
		}
```
```

> AGENT

Fixed and pushed. Now regarding your question about the feature flag — yes, Nostr is behind a feature flag like other channels. The chain is:

- `crates/cli/Cargo.toml`: `nostr = ["moltis-httpd/nostr"]` (in `default`)
- `crates/httpd/Cargo.toml`: `nostr = ["moltis-gateway/nostr"]` (in `default`)
- `crates/gateway/Cargo.toml`: `nostr = ["dep:moltis-nostr"]` (in `default`), plus `moltis-nostr?/metrics` in the `metrics` feature
- `crates/gateway/src/server.rs`: registration under `#[cfg(feature = "nostr")]`

Same pattern as `matrix`, `slack`, and `whatsapp`.
