ID: 3069560053
File: crates/nostr/src/bus.rs:195
Body: <a href="#"><img alt="P1" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p1.svg?v=7" align="top"></a> **OTP challenge never initiated or sent**

When `otp_self_approval = true` (the default) and a non-allowlisted sender DMs the bot, the bus emits `InboundMessage { access_granted: false }` and returns — but it never calls `state.otp.initiate()` to generate a code, never sends the code back to the sender via an outbound DM, and `pending_otp_challenges()` always returns empty because `AccountState.otp` is never written to. The OTP self-approval path is silently broken for all Nostr accounts.

Telegram's equivalent in `crates/telegram/src/handlers.rs` shows the full pattern: it passes an `Arc<Mutex<OtpState>>` into the event handler, calls `otp.initiate(peer_id, ...)` to generate the code, then sends it to the user with `emit_otp_challenge(...)`. Nostr's `handle_event` receives neither the OTP state nor the outbound sender needed to complete this flow.

Concrete failure: with the shipped default config (`dm_policy = Allowlist`, `otp_self_approval = true`), any new user DM is silently dropped with zero feedback — the user never receives an OTP code and has no path to gaining access.
```

Per-account runtime state for Nostr.\n\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\nuse {\n    moltis_channels::otp::OtpState,\n    nostr_sdk::prelude::{Client, Keys, PublicKey, ToBech32},\n    tokio::sync::RwLock,\n    tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken,\n};\n\nuse crate::config::NostrAccountConfig;\n\n/// Shared config reference — the bus loop and plugin both read/write through\n/// this same `Arc` so runtime config updates (DM policy, allowlist) take\n/// effect immediately without restarting the account.\npub type SharedConfig = Arc<RwLock<NostrAccountConfig>>;\n\n/// Shared OTP state — bus loop initiates challenges, plugin reads pending list.\npub type SharedOtp = Arc<Mutex<OtpState>>;\n\n/// Runtime state for a single active Nostr account.\npub struct AccountState {\n    /// The nostr-sdk client connected to relays.\n    pub client: Client,\n    /// Bot key pair (secret + public).\n    pub keys: Keys,\n    /// Shared account configuration — same Arc given to the bus loop.\n    pub config: SharedConfig,\n    /// Pre-parsed allowlist pubkeys, refreshed on config update.\n    pub cached_allowlist: Arc<RwLock<Vec<PublicKey>>>,\n    /// Cancellation token for the subscription loop.\n    pub cancel: CancellationToken,\n    /// OTP self-approval state — shared with bus loop.\n    pub otp: SharedOtp,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Debug for AccountState {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        let pk = self\n            .keys\n            .public_key()\n            .to_bech32()\n            .unwrap_or_else(|_| self.keys.public_key().to_hex());\n        f.debug_struct(\"AccountState\")\n            .field(\"pubkey\", &pk)\n            .finish_non_exhaustive()\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "content": "//! Nostr relay subscription loop — inbound DM pipeline.\n//!\n//! Subscribes to kind:4 (NIP-04 encrypted DMs) addressed to the bot's pubkey.\n//! Events flow through dedup, self-message filtering, access control, and\n//! decryption before being dispatched to the gateway via `ChannelEventSink`.\n\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse {\n    nostr_sdk::prelude::{\n        Client, Event, Filter, Keys, Kind, PublicKey, RelayPoolNotification, Timestamp, ToBech32,\n        nip04, nip44,\n    },\n    tokio::sync::RwLock,\n    tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken,\n};\n\nuse crate::{\n    access::{self, AccessDenied},\n    config::NostrAccountConfig,\n    seen::SeenTracker,\n    state::SharedOtp,\n};\n\n#[cfg(feature = \"metrics\")]\nuse moltis_metrics::{counter, nostr as nostr_metrics};\n\n/// Maximum plaintext message size in bytes.\nconst MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024;\n\n/// Message sent to non-allowlisted senders as an OTP challenge prompt.\nconst OTP_CHALLENGE_MSG: &str =\n    \"You are not on the allowlist. A PIN challenge has been sent to the admin. Reply with the 6-digit code to gain access.\";\n\n/// Run the relay subscription loop for a single Nostr account.\n///\n/// Subscribes to NIP-04 DMs (kind:4) targeted at `bot_pubkey` and dispatches\n/// inbound messages to the gateway. Runs until `cancel` is triggered or the\n/// relay pool shuts down (which triggers an auto-disable request).\npub async fn run_subscription_loop(\n    client: Client,\n    keys: Keys,\n    config: Arc<RwLock<NostrAccountConfig>>,\n    cached_allowlist: Arc<RwLock<Vec<PublicKey>>>,\n    otp: SharedOtp,\n    account_id: String,\n    event_sink: Arc<dyn moltis_channels::ChannelEventSink>,\n    cancel: CancellationToken,\n) {\n    let bot_pubkey = keys.public_key();\n    let now_secs =\n        u64::try_from(::time::OffsetDateTime::now_utc().unix_timestamp()).unwrap_or_default();\n    let since = Timestamp::from(now_secs);\n\n    let filter = Filter::new()\n        .kind(Kind::EncryptedDirectMessage)\n        .pubkey(bot_pubkey)\n        .since(since);\n\n    let npub = bot_pubkey\n        .to_bech32()\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| bot_pubkey.to_hex());\n    tracing::info!(\n        account_id,\n        pubkey = %npub,\n        \"starting Nostr DM subscription\"\n    );\n\n    let mut seen = SeenTracker::new();\n\n    // Subscribe (single filter)\n    if let Err(e) = client.subscribe(filter, None).await {\n        tracing::error!(account_id, \"failed to subscribe: {e}\");\n        return;\n    }\n\n    let mut notifications = client.notifications();\n\n    loop {\n        tokio::select! {\n            () = cancel.cancelled() => {\n                tracing::info!(account_id, \"Nostr subscription cancelled\");\n                break;\n            }\n            notification = notifications.recv() => {\n                match notification {\n                    Ok(RelayPoolNotification::Event { event, .. }) => {\n                        handle_event(\n                            &event,\n                            &client,\n                            &keys,\n                            &bot_pubkey,\n                            since,\n                            &mut seen,\n                            &config,\n                            &cached_allowlist,\n                            &otp,\n                            &account_id,\n                            &event_sink,\n                        ).await;\n                    }\n                    Ok(RelayPoolNotification::Shutdown) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(account_id, \"relay pool shutdown — requesting account disable\");\n                        event_sink\n                            .request_disable_account(\"nostr\", &account_id, \"relay pool shutdown\")\n                            .await;\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    Ok(_) => {}\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(account_id, \"notification channel error: {e}\");\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    tracing::info!(account_id, \"Nostr subscription loop exited\");\n}\n\n/// Process a single inbound event through the pipeline.\n#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\nasync fn handle_event(\n    event: &Event,\n    client: &Client,\n    keys: &Keys,\n    bot_pubkey: &PublicKey,\n    since: Timestamp,\n    seen: &mut SeenTracker,\n    config: &Arc<RwLock<NostrAccountConfig>>,\n    cached_allowlist: &Arc<RwLock<Vec<PublicKey>>>,\n    otp: &SharedOtp,\n    account_id: &str,\n    event_sink: &Arc<dyn moltis_channels::ChannelEventSink>,\n) {\n    // 1. Skip non-DM events\n    if event.kind != Kind::EncryptedDirectMessage {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // 2. Dedup check\n    if seen.check_and_insert(&event.id) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // 3. Skip self-messages\n    if event.pubkey == *bot_pubkey {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // 4. Skip stale events\n    if event.created_at < since {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // 5. Access control (BEFORE decryption).\n    //    Read the config and cached allowlist, extract what we need, then drop\n    //    the guards before any `.await` to avoid holding RwLockReadGuard across\n    //    yield points.\n    let (dm_policy, otp_self_approval) = {\n        let cfg = config.read().await;\n        (cfg.dm_policy.clone(), cfg.otp_self_approval)\n    };\n\n    let allowed = cached_allowlist.read().await;\n    let access_result = access::check_dm_access(&event.pubkey, &dm_policy, &allowed);\n    drop(allowed);\n\n    let sender_hex = event.pubkey.to_hex();\n    let sender_npub = event\n        .pubkey\n        .to_bech32()\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| sender_hex.clone());\n\n    match &access_result {\n        Ok(()) => {},\n        Err(AccessDenied::Disabled) => {\n            #[cfg(feature = \"metrics\")]\n            counter!(nostr_metrics::ACCESS_CONTROL_DENIALS_TOTAL, \"reason\" => \"disabled\")\n                .increment(1);\n            tracing::debug!(account_id, sender = sender_hex, \"DM rejected: disabled\");\n            return;\n        },\n        Err(AccessDenied::NotAllowlisted) => {\n            #[cfg(feature = \"metrics\")]\n            counter!(nostr_metrics::ACCESS_CONTROL_DENIALS_TOTAL, \"reason\" => \"not_allowlisted\")\n                .increment(1);\n            if otp_self_approval {\n                handle_otp_challenge(\n                    client,\n                    keys,\n                    &event.pubkey,\n                    otp,\n                    account_id,\n                    &sender_hex,\n                    &sender_npub,\n                    event_sink,\n                )\n                .await;\n            } else {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    account_id,\n                    sender = sender_hex,\n                    \"DM rejected: not allowlisted\"\n                );\n            }\n            return;\n        },\n    }\n\n    // 6. Decrypt content — try NIP-04 first, fall back to NIP-44\n    let plaintext = match nip04::decrypt(keys.secret_key(), &event.pubkey, &event.content) {\n        Ok(text) => text,\n        Err(_nip04_err) => {\n            match nip44::decrypt(keys.secret_key(), &event.pubkey, &event.content) {\n                Ok(text) => text,\n                Err(nip44_err) => {\n                    #[cfg(feature = \"metrics\")]\n                    counter!(nostr_metrics::DECRYPT_ERRORS_TOTAL).increment(1);\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        account_id,\n                        event_id = %event.id,\n                        \"decrypt failed (NIP-04 and NIP-44): {nip44_err}\"\n                    );\n                    return;\n                },\n            }\n        },\n    };\n\n    // 7. Size validation — truncate at a safe UTF-8 boundary\n    let text = if plaintext.len() > MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES {\n        tracing::warn!(account_id, len = plaintext.len(), \"DM exceeds size limit\");\n        &plaintext[..plaintext.floor_char_boundary(MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES)]\n    } else {\n        &plaintext\n    };\n\n    // 8. Emit inbound event\n    #[cfg(feature = \"metrics\")]\n    counter!(nostr_metrics::MESSAGES_RECEIVED_TOTAL).increment(1);\n\n    event_sink\n        .emit(moltis_channels::ChannelEvent::InboundMessage {\n            channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n            account_id: account_id.to_string(),\n            peer_id: sender_hex.clone(),\n            username: Some(sender_npub.clone()),\n            sender_name: None,\n            message_count: None,\n            access_granted: true,\n        })\n        .await;\n\n    // 9. Dispatch to gateway\n    let reply_to = moltis_channels::ChannelReplyTarget {\n        channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n        account_id: account_id.to_string(),\n        chat_id: sender_hex,\n        message_id: Some(event.id.to_hex()),\n        thread_id: None,\n    };\n\n    let meta = moltis_channels::ChannelMessageMeta {\n        channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n        sender_name: None,\n        username: Some(sender_npub),\n        message_kind: Some(moltis_channels::ChannelMessageKind::Text),\n        model: None,\n        audio_filename: None,\n    };\n\n    event_sink.dispatch_to_chat(text, reply_to, meta).await;\n}\n\n/// Initiate an OTP challenge for a non-allowlisted sender.\n///\n/// Generates a 6-digit code via `OtpState::initiate()`, sends the challenge\n/// prompt to the sender as an encrypted DM, and emits an `OtpChallenge` event\n/// for the admin web UI.\n#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\nasync fn handle_otp_challenge(\n    client: &Client,\n    keys: &Keys,\n    sender_pubkey: &PublicKey,\n    otp: &SharedOtp,\n    account_id: &str,\n    sender_hex: &str,\n    sender_npub: &str,\n    event_sink: &Arc<dyn moltis_channels::ChannelEventSink>,\n) {\n    use moltis_channels::otp::{OtpInitResult, emit_otp_challenge};\n\n    let init_result = {\n        let mut otp_guard = otp.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());\n        otp_guard.initiate(sender_hex, Some(sender_npub.to_string()), None)\n    };\n\n    match init_result {\n        OtpInitResult::Created(code) => {\n            // Send challenge prompt to the sender via encrypted DM.\n            if let Ok(encrypted) =\n                nip04::encrypt(keys.secret_key(), sender_pubkey, OTP_CHALLENGE_MSG)\n            {\n                let tag = nostr_sdk::prelude::Tag::public_key(*sender_pubkey);\n                let builder = nostr_sdk::prelude::EventBuilder::new(\n                    Kind::EncryptedDirectMessage,\n                    &encrypted,\n                )\n                .tag(tag);\n                if let Err(e) = client.send_event_builder(builder).await {\n                    tracing::warn!(account_id, \"failed to send OTP challenge DM: {e}\");\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Emit OTP challenge event for the admin UI.\n            let expires_at = ::time::OffsetDateTime::now_utc().unix_timestamp() + 300;\n\n            emit_otp_challenge(\n                Some(event_sink.as_ref()),\n                moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n                account_id,\n                sender_hex,\n                Some(sender_npub),\n                None,\n                code,\n                expires_at,\n            )\n            .await;\n\n            #[cfg(feature = \"metrics\")]\n            counter!(nostr_metrics::OTP_CHALLENGES_TOTAL).increment(1);\n        },\n        OtpInitResult::AlreadyPending | OtpInitResult::LockedOut => {\n            // Silent — don't spam the sender.\n        },\n    }\n\n    // Always emit InboundMessage with access_granted: false for the UI.\n    event_sink\n        .emit(moltis_channels::ChannelEvent::InboundMessage {\n            channel_type: moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n            account_id: account_id.to_string(),\n            peer_id: sender_hex.to_string(),\n            username: Some(sender_npub.to_string()),\n            sender_name: None,\n            message_count: None,\n            access_granted: false,\n        })\n        .await;\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn max_message_size_is_reasonable() {\n        assert_eq!(MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES, 64 * 1024);\n    }\n}\n"

<a href="#"><img alt="P1" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p1.svg?v=7" align="top"></a> **OTP verification path never reached**

The `handle_otp_challenge` function correctly initiates challenges, but the bus loop never calls `otp.verify()`. When a non-allowlisted sender responds with the 6-digit code, `check_dm_access` still returns `Err(NotAllowlisted)` (they aren't on the allowlist yet), `handle_otp_challenge` is called again, `otp.initiate()` returns `AlreadyPending`, and the message is silently dropped. With the default config (`dm_policy = Allowlist`, `otp_self_approval = true`), no user can ever complete the OTP flow.

Telegram's pattern in `crates/telegram/src/handlers.rs` shows what's needed: before the access-control branch, check `otp.has_pending(sender_hex)`. If pending and the decrypted message is a 6-digit code, call `otp.verify()` and handle `Approved`/`WrongCode`/`LockedOut`/`Expired` — the decryption step must move above the access-control gate for this to work.

```rust
// After dedup / self-msg / stale checks, before access control:
let (dm_policy, otp_self_approval) = {
    let cfg = config.read().await;
    (cfg.dm_policy.clone(), cfg.otp_self_approval)
};

// 5a. OTP verification (must decrypt first to inspect the code)
let has_pending = {
    let guard = otp.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    guard.has_pending(&sender_hex)
};
if has_pending {
    let plaintext = /* decrypt ... */;
    let trimmed = plaintext.trim();
    if trimmed.len() == 6 && trimmed.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {
        let result = {
            let mut guard = otp.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
            guard.verify(&sender_hex, trimmed)
        };
        // handle Approved / WrongCode / LockedOut / Expired ...
        return;
    }
    return; // non-code reply while challenge pending → silent ignore
}

// 5b. Normal access control gate
let access_result = access::check_dm_access(&event.pubkey, &dm_policy, &allowed);
// ... rest of existing logic
```

Send another message to get a new code.\",\n            \"expired\",\n        ),\n    };\n\n    // Send the reply to the sender.\n    if let Ok(encrypted) = nip04::encrypt(keys.secret_key(), sender_pubkey, reply_text) {\n        let tag = nostr_sdk::prelude::Tag::public_key(*sender_pubkey);\n        let builder =\n            nostr_sdk::prelude::EventBuilder::new(Kind::EncryptedDirectMessage, &encrypted)\n                .tag(tag);\n        if let Err(e) = client.send_event_builder(builder).await {\n            tracing::warn!(account_id, \"failed to send OTP verification reply: {e}\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Emit resolution event for admin UI.\n    emit_otp_resolution(\n        Some(event_sink.as_ref()),\n        moltis_channels::ChannelType::Nostr,\n        account_id,\n        sender_hex,\n        Some(sender_npub),\n        resolution,\n    )\n    .await;\n}\n\n/// Initiate an OTP challenge for a non-allowlisted sender."
}

Telegram uses `std::sync::RwLock`, not `tokio::sync::RwLock`. The Nostr crate uses `tokio::sync::RwLock` for the account map which panics with `blocking_read()` from within a tokio runtime. I need to switch the `AccountStateMap` to use `std::sync::RwLock`.

The `SharedConfig` inside each account can remain `tokio::sync::RwLock` since it's only accessed with `.await` in the bus loop. But the outer account map must be `std::sync::RwLock`.

> AGENT
